old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:14 — *a faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure. Nothing doth countervail a faithful friend.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the supreme-worth-substance the buyer pays-all-to-obtain; Matt 13:45-46 names the operative-form at the pearl-of-great-price register.
new: Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* The one pearl worth all the merchant had, Matthew 13:45.

old: Sirach 6:28 — *at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* The second Sirach yoke-passage (Sirach 6:24-31) naming the rest-yielded-by-the-yoke-of-wisdom architecture; the same shape Matt 11:29's *ye shall find rest unto your souls* walks.
new: Ecclesiasticus 6:28 — *at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* The rest found under the yoke at Matthew 11:29.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:4 — *Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the seek-not-preeminence substance the King walks-against at Matt 23:6 (*love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues*).
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:4 — *Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.* The chief seats loved at Matthew 23:6.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:23 — *have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the parental-instruction-of-children substance — the substance the parents-bringing-the-little-children-to-the-King at Matt 19:13 enact at the practical-substance level, in continuity with Devarim (Deuteronomy) 6:6-7 + Tehillim (Psalm) 78:5-7.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:23 — *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* The parents bringing their children to Yahusha (Jesus) at Matthew 19:13.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:27 — *honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.* The wisdom-stream's articulation at the heart-level — the whole-heart-honor architecture the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition violated by establishing a divided-heart-allowed-by-the-vow-mechanism. The King's-restoration of the heart-substance at vv.18-20 closes the loop on the heart-level the wisdom-stream had named.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:27 — *Honour your father with your whole heart.* The whole heart the corban tradition divided, against Matthew 15:4.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:30 — *love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the love-Yahuah-with-all-thy-strength substance — Sirach 7:30 carries the Shema-substance of Devarim (Deuteronomy) 6:5 forward at the wisdom-stream-register; the substance the King cites at Matt 22:37.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:30 — *Love him that made you with all your strength.* The Shema the Messiah quotes at Matthew 22:37, carried forward by Sirach.

old: Proverbs 3:9 — *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase* — the firstfruits-portion Sirach 7:31 names among the priest's due.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:31 — *give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits.* The firstfruits that honor Yahuah (LORD) in Proverbs 3:9 reach him through the priest's hand.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:32 — *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* The stretch-your-hand-to-the-poor substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the substantial-criterion-of-mercy. Sirach 7:32-35 walks the same six-fold-substance with *fail not to be with them that weep* (v.34) and *be not slow to visit the sick* (v.35); the substantial-substance is the substantial-blessing-being-perfected through the substantial-doing.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:32 — *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* The hand stretched to the poor is the measure the King uses at Matthew 25:36.

old: Matthew 5:28 — *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* the Messiah taking Sirach 9:8's turn-away-the-eye to the heart's root.
new: Ecclesiasticus 9:8 — *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman.* The eye turned away in Sirach is the heart Yahusha (Jesus) reads at Matthew 5:28.

old: Sirach 9:10 — *forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him.* The wisdom-stream holds the old-vs-new in inverse register to the gospel; the Pharisaic-rabbinic-system's self-justification rests on the wisdom-stream loyalty. The Torah is NEITHER the wine NOR the wineskin; the rabbinic-old-bottle bursts when the heart-Torah-life enters.
new: Ecclesiasticus 9:10 — *a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach's new wine that ages well sits beside the new wine and new bottles of Matthew 9:17.

old: Proverbs 13:20 — *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* the consult-with-the-wise counsel of Sirach 9:14-15.
new: Ecclesiasticus 9:14 — *guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.* Sirach's consult with the wise is Solomon's walk with wise men at Proverbs 13:20.

old: Psalm 1:2 — *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* the law-of-the-Most-High talk Sirach 9:15 says fills the wise man's communication.
new: Ecclesiasticus 9:15 — *all your communication in the law of the Most High.* Talk in the law of the Most High is the delight in the law of Psalm 1:2 spoken aloud.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10:7 — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the disposition-the-King-is-confronting at the disciples' Matt 18:1 hierarchy-question — the pride-substance operating-in the disciples' road-side-dispute (Mark 9:33-34's *who should be the greatest*); the King's-acted-parable of the child-in-the-midst is the substance-correction the wisdom-stream had instructed-toward.
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:7 — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man.* The pride Sirach names is the disposition behind who is the greatest at Matthew 18:1.

old: Sirach 10:12 — *the beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.* The heart-turned-away root; Luke 11:46's burden-lading lawyers walk the parallel-Torah-built-on-top the heart-turned-away produces.
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:12 — *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God).* The heart turned from its Maker is the lawyer lading burdens at Luke 11:46.

old: Sirach 10:13 — *pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* The pride-as-sin's-beginning fruit; Luke 11:43's love-of-the-uppermost-seats is the religious-status pride Sirach diagnosed.
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination.* The pride that begins sin is the love of the uppermost seats at Luke 11:43.

old: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* Ben Sira's own diagnosis self-linking pride=the-beginning-of-sin to the proud abhorred in Sirach 16:8.
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* The strange calamities of pride land on the place where Lot sojourned at Ecclesiasticus 16:8.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10:14 — *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the kingdom-inversion-of-thrones substance — the proud-cast-down and the meek-set-up at the same divine-action; the substance the assembly is to walk-in at Matt 18:4 is the substance the Father acts-by at the eschatological-day, with the apostolic-restatement at Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:51-52) and 1 Corinthians 1:26-29 (*Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise*).
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:14 — *cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The meek set up in the proud's stead is the child who is greatest at Matthew 18:4.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10:14 — *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the kingdom-inversion-substance the King names at Matt 23:12 (*whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted*).
new: Ecclesiasticus 10:14 — *cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The thrones changing hands is the rule of Matthew 23:12 written as history.

old: Sirach 11:14 — *prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).* The all-comes-of-Yahuah architecture; Matt 6:33's *all these things shall be added unto you* walks the same source-of-all teaching.
new: Ecclesiasticus 11:14 — *Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).* Because both come of Yahuah (God), the citizen can seek first the kingdom at Matthew 6:33.

old: Sirach 11:18 — *there is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* The hollow-reward of the hoarder; Luke 12:20's *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be?* lands the reckoning the wisdom-stream set up.
new: Ecclesiasticus 11:18 — *waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward.* The hoarder's whole reward is the heap left behind when the soul is required at Luke 12:20.

old: Sirach 11:19 — *whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.* The Hebrew library names the rich fool word-for-word; Luke 12:19's *take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* walks the same architecture, and the two things the fool ignores — the unknown hour and the leaving-to-others — are exactly what the verdict names.
new: Ecclesiasticus 11:19 — *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods.* Sirach's rich man speaks the rich fool's line of Luke 12:19 centuries early.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:21 — *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour.* The trust-and-abide-in-your-labour substance — the substantial-substance the faithful-servants walk-out at the doubling of the talents at Matt 25:16-23; the substantial-faithfulness (NOT the substantial-comparative-quantity) is the Father-substance's-criterion.
new: Ecclesiasticus 11:21 — *trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour.* Abiding in the labour is what earns well done, thou good and faithful servant at Matthew 25:21.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:26 — *for it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.* The direct verbal-anchor for the reward-according-to-his-ways substance the substantial-faithful-and-wise-servant walks-into at Matt 24:46 — the substantial-reward is according-to-the-substantial-ways the substantial-substance has-walked-through the substantial-period of the lord's-delay.
new: Ecclesiasticus 11:26 — *in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.* Reward according to his ways is the servant found so doing at Matthew 24:46.

old: Sirach 12:4 — *give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* The wisdom-stream's discriminating-mercy stance the Pharisaic-counterfeit-righteousness inherited; Matt 9:10's King-at-the-table-with-sinners is the direct-reversal.
new: Ecclesiasticus 12:4 — *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach guards the hand from strengthening the ungodly; the King's table at Matthew 9:10 calls sinners to turn.

old: Sirach 12:5 — *hold back your bread, and give it not to the ungodly.* The wisdom-stream's explicit instruction the Pharisees at Matt 9:11 are operating under; the King breaks the discriminating-bread-fellowship rule by eating with those Sirach 12 instructed his disciples to hold-back-from.
new: Ecclesiasticus 12:5 — *hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby.* Bread held back from the one who would overmaster you is not the table the Pharisees question at Matthew 9:11.

old: Sirach 12:7 — *give to the good, and help not the sinner.* The wisdom-stream's categorical-exclusion the King reverses at Matt 9:13: *not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance* is the inverse of the Sirach 12 mandate.
new: Ecclesiasticus 12:7 — *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Help not the sinner and call sinners to repentance (Matthew 9:13) meet at the word repentance.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12:16 — *an enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit.* The substantial-enemy-who-speaks-sweetly-with-the-lips-while-imagining-the-pit substance — the substantial-Yahudah-Iscariot (Judas Iscariot)'s kiss at Matt 26:49 (*Hail, master; and kissed him*) walks-substantively in continuity with Proverbs 27:6's *the kisses of an enemy are deceitful* + Psalm 55:12-14.
new: Ecclesiasticus 12:16 — *An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit.* The enemy with sweet lips is Judas with Hail, master, and a kiss at Matthew 26:49.

old: Sirach 14:8 — *the envious man has a wicked eye; he turns away his face, and despiseth men.* The Hebrew library's direct *wicked eye* = envious / stingy idiom; Matt 6:23's *evil eye* walks the same Hebrew-idiom architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 14:8 — *The envious man has a wicked eye.* Sirach's wicked eye of envy is the evil eye that darkens the body at Matthew 6:23.

old: Sirach 14:9 — *a covetous man's eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul.* The grasping-heart diagnostic; Matt 6:23's *whole body full of darkness* walks the same architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 14:9 — *A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion.* The unsatisfied eye that dries the soul is the evil eye of Matthew 6:23.

old: Sirach 14:10 — *a wicked eye envies his bread, and he is a niggard at his table.* The wicked-eye-at-the-table architecture — closed-heart hospitality; Matt 6:23's *how great is that darkness!* names the intensity of the same diagnostic.
new: Ecclesiasticus 14:10 — *A wicked eye envies his bread, and he is a niggard at his table.* The niggard's table is the darkness of Matthew 6:23 with bread on it.

old: Job 1:21 — *And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Job's surrender frames the do-good-to-thyself-and-give-Yahuah-his-due of Sirach 14:11.
new: Ecclesiasticus 14:11 — *according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.* Give Yahuah (God) his due while it is in your hand; Job 1:21 says who gave it and who takes it.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:11 — *say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father-NOT-being-the-source-of-the-man's-falling-away substance the King's-restoration of the heart-and-mouth-substance-as-the-locus-of-defilement enacts at vv.10-20.
new: Ecclesiasticus 15:11 — *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away.* The fall is not from Yahuah (God), and the defilement is not from the food (Matthew 15:11); both come from the man.

old: Proverbs 15:3 — *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.* Sirach's all-beholding Yahuah (Sirach 15:18) is the proverb's eyes-in-every-place.
new: Ecclesiasticus 15:18 — *he is mighty in power, and beholds all things.* Sirach's all-beholding Yahuah (God) is the eyes in every place of Proverbs 15:3.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:20 — *he has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the Father-NOT-commanding-wickedness-and-NOT-giving-licence-to-sin substance — therefore the source-of-the-wickedness IS NOT-the-Father; the source IS the man's-own-heart the King names at Matt 15:18-19.
new: Ecclesiasticus 15:20 — *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* No licence to sin from Yahuah (God); the sin comes out of the heart at Matthew 15:18.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 16:12 — *as his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works.* The wisdom-stream's headline-articulation of the Father-judges-a-man-according-to-his-works substance — both the mercy and the correction operating from the Father's-righteous-character.
new: Ecclesiasticus 16:12 — *he judges a man according to his works.* Judged according to his works is the Son of Adam's reward at Matthew 16:27.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 16:14 — *every man shall find according to his works.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the universal-substance — every man finds according to his works at the day-of-judgment the King's-Son-of-Adam-coming substance enacts.
new: Ecclesiasticus 16:14 — *Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.* Every man finds according to his works when the Son of Adam comes at Matthew 16:27.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 16:14 — *make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.* The every-man-shall-find-according-to-his-works substance — the substantial-greater-stewardship at Matt 24:47 walks-the-architecture-of (*make him ruler over all his goods*); the substantial-substance against the inherited-Reformation-eternal-security-substance — the substantial-substance is the walking-out-of-the-works the Spirit-internalized-Torah walks per the new-heart of Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27.
new: Ecclesiasticus 16:14 — *every man shall find according to his works.* Finding according to works is the servant made ruler over all his goods at Matthew 24:47.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:3 — *he endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the image-of-Elohim-stamped-on-man substance — Sirach 17 carries the Bereshit (Genesis) 1:26-27 creation-substance forward; the citizen bears the image-of-Elohim the same way the coin at Matt 22:20 bears Caesar's image.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:3 — *made them according to his image.* The image stamped on man is the image the King asks about at Matthew 22:20.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:11 — *beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the law-of-life-as-heritage substance — the architecture the King's-own-mouth at Matt 19:17 stands on (*if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments*), the FRAMEWORK-MAJOR-LOADING moment against Red Line #2's antinomian-Paul reading.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:11 — *the law of life for an heritage.* The law of life is the keep the commandments that enters into life at Matthew 19:17.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:11 — *beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* The wisdom-stream articulation of the law-of-life-for-an-heritage substance — the Torah given to the citizen-stamped-with-the-Father's-image as inheritance; per Red Line #4, Torah is NOT the curse but the covenant-inheritance the citizen renders-back-to-the-Father at Matt 22:21 (*unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's)*).
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:11 — *he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* The law of life given as heritage is among the things that are Elohim's (God's) at Matthew 22:21.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:14 — *beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the commandment-concerning-the-neighbor substance — Sirach 17:14 carries the Vayikra (Leviticus) 19:18 substance forward and names the architecture explicitly; the substance the King cites at Matt 22:39 as the second-commandment.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:14 — *he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* The commandment concerning the neighbour is the second great commandment of Matthew 22:39.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:24 — *but to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* THE direct verbal-anchor for the *to-them-that-repent-he-granted-them-return* substance the first-son-substance walks at Matt 21:29 (*I will not: but afterward he repented, and went*); the publicans-and-harlots-substance walks the wisdom-stream-substance the Father grants-return-to.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:24 — *to them that repent, he granted them return.* Return granted to them that repent is the son who afterward repented, and went at Matthew 21:29.

old: Ezekiel 18:32 — *For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.* The mercy granting return in Sirach 17:24 is Yahuah's no-pleasure-in-death heart.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:24 — *to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* Return granted to the penitent is the no pleasure in the death of him that dieth of Ezekiel 18:32.

old: James 4:8 — *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* 'Make your prayer before his face, and offend less' (Sirach 17:25) is James' draw-nigh-and-cleanse summons.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:25 — *make your prayer before his face, and offend less.* Prayer before his face and offending less is James's draw nigh and cleanse your hands at James 4:8.

old: Ezekiel 18:30 — *Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.* Sirach 17:26 'turn away from iniquity' is Ezekiel's turn-and-be-saved call.
new: Ecclesiasticus 17:26 — *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity.* Turn away from iniquity is Ezekiel's so iniquity shall not be your ruin at Ezekiel 18:30.

old: Psalm 103:15 — *As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.* The hundred-year span of Sirach 18:9 is the same flower-of-the-field brevity the Psalmist sings.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:9 — *The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.* A hundred years at the most is the flower of the field of Psalm 103:15.

old: Sirach 18:13 — *the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The shepherd-who-brings-again-his-flock; Luke 15:5's *he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing* walks the same bringing-again-the-lost substance.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The bringing again is the lost sheep carried home on the shepherd's shoulders (Luke 15:5).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 18:13 — *the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The Father's own shepherding-architecture; John 21:16's *feed my sheep* hands that reprove-and-bring-again charge to the restored Peter for the flock.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* The Father's own shepherding, handed to the restored Peter in *Feed my sheep* (John 21:16).

old: Psalm 145:9 — *Yahuah (LORD) is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.* This is the mercy-upon-all-flesh of Sirach 18:13 word for word — tender mercies over all His works.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh.* The tender mercies over all his works in Psalm 145:9, said again.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 18:14 — *he has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.* The mercy-on-the-disciplined register; Peter, grieved at the third asking, receives the discipline of the threefold question and the mercy lands as the charge to feed the sheep.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:14 — *He has mercy on them that receive discipline.* Peter, grieved at the third asking, receives the discipline and the mercy lands as *Feed my sheep* (John 21:17).

old: James 1:19 — *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.* Ya'akov's swift-to-hear is Sirach 18:19's learn-before-you-speak in the same wisdom stream.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:19 — *Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.* Learning before speaking is James' *swift to hear, slow to speak* (James 1:19).

old: Ecclesiastes 5:4 — *When thou vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.* Qoheleth's defer-not-thy-vow is the very law Sirach 18:22 echoes — pay in due time, defer not till death.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:22 — *Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time.* The rule of Ecclesiastes 5:4, *defer not to pay it*, carried into Sirach's counsel.

old: Galatians 5:16 — *This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.* Sha'ul's Spirit-walk is Sirach 18:30's refrain-thyself-from-thy-appetites.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:30 — *Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.* The refraining Sirach commands is done by walking in the Spirit (Galatians 5:16).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 19:13 — *Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it: and if he have done it, that he may do it no more.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the King's first-step assembly-discipline pattern at Matt 18:15 — confront-privately FIRST, with the substance aimed at restoration (*it may be he has not done it*; *he may do it no more*), in continuity with Vayikra (Leviticus) 19:17's Tanakh-substance of private-rebuke-to-the-neighbour.
new: Ecclesiasticus 19:13 — *Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it.* The private first step of Matthew 18:15 — go to him alone, and he may be gained.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 19:15 — *Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.* The substance the witness-verification-procedure at Matt 18:16 protects against — slander, the false-tale, the unverified-charge. The King applies the Devarim (Deuteronomy) 19:15 two-or-three-witnesses Tanakh-standard the wisdom-stream had named the necessity-of; the witnesses protect both the brother-accused AND the brother-accusing from the corruptions either could fall into.
new: Ecclesiasticus 19:15 — *for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.* The two or three witnesses of Matthew 18:16 guard against the slander Sirach warns of.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 19:17 — *Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the Most High.* The order (admonish BEFORE threatening) AND the inner-disposition (not-being-angry, giving-place-to-the-Torah-of-the-Most-High) — the same disposition the King's assembly-discipline procedure carries from v.15's private-rebuke through v.17's assembly-level-confrontation; the apostolic-restatement at Galatians 6:1 — *restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.*
new: Ecclesiasticus 19:17 — *Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him.* The order and the temper of the private word in Matthew 18:15 — admonish first, and not in anger.

old: Matthew 7:16 — *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* Sira's 'a man may be known by his look' is Yeshua's know-them-by-fruits: the inward deceit shows itself outwardly.
new: Ecclesiasticus 19:29 — *A man may be known by his look.* What is inward shows outwardly; *Ye shall know them by their fruits* (Matthew 7:16).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20:2 — *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt.* The architecture under the King's step-three assembly-level-confrontation at Matt 18:17 — the wisdom-stream names the alternative-architecture (angry-secretly is the substance that does-not-restore) and the operative-architecture (open-reproof followed-by-confession is the substance that restores); the assembly-as-a-whole carries the open-reproof at the corporate-register the wisdom-stream had carried at the wisdom-instruction-register.
new: Ecclesiasticus 20:2 — *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly.* The open reproof before the assembly in Matthew 18:17 — the alternative to secret anger that restores no one.

old: Proverbs 17:28 — *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* The same paradox Ben Sira sets down in Sirach 20:5 — silence itself confers the appearance, and the substance, of wisdom.
new: Ecclesiasticus 20:5 — *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise.* The same paradox as Proverbs 17:28 — the fool who holds his peace is counted wise.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20:30 — *wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the hidden-treasure-and-finding-and-obtaining substance; Matt 13:44's treasure-hid-in-the-field names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register.
new: Ecclesiasticus 20:30 — *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both.* The treasure hid in the field is found and bought with everything (Matthew 13:44).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 21:1 — *my son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the *ask-pardon-for-your-former-sins* substance the Yochanan (John)-baptism walked-out at the wilderness-pericope — the substance the publicans-and-harlots walked-into at Matt 21:32 and the chief-priests-and-elders refused-to-walk.
new: Ecclesiasticus 21:1 — *have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* The repentance John preached — the publicans and harlots did it, the office refused it (Matthew 21:32).

old: Proverbs 9:6 — *Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.* The turn-and-sin-no-more wisdom of Ben Sira's opening call (Ecclesiasticus 21:1).
new: Ecclesiasticus 21:1 — *do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* The turn Wisdom calls for in Proverbs 9:6 — forsake the foolish, and live.

old: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* The fear-of-Yahuah-is-wisdom refrain Ben Sira makes the crown of law-keeping (Ecclesiasticus 21:11).
new: Ecclesiasticus 21:11 — *He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof.* The fear of Yahuah (LORD) that begins wisdom in Proverbs 9:10 is made perfect in keeping the law.

old: Sirach 21:14 — *the inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.* The broken-vessel heart that holds no knowledge; Luke 11:52's lawyers took away the key of knowledge because they hold none themselves.
new: Ecclesiasticus 21:14 — *The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel.* The lawyers who took away the key of knowledge held none themselves (Luke 11:52).

old: Sirach 21:15 — *as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* The man-of-no-understanding casting the wise word behind his back; Luke 11:52's taking-away-the-key is that casting-the-word-behind-the-back, then locking the door against those entering.
new: Ecclesiasticus 21:15 — *it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* The word cast behind the back, then the key of knowledge taken away from those entering (Luke 11:52).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 22:1 — *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* THE direct verbal-anchor for the slothful-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) names at the unprofitable-servant at Matt 25:26 (Greek *oknēre* — slothful, hesitating, shrinking), in continuity with Proverbs 6:6-11, 13:4, 19:15, 24:30-34. The substantial-non-action is the substantial-substance the Father-substance walks-against.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:1 — *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone.* The *wicked and slothful servant* of Matthew 25:26 — the work left undone is the disgrace.

old: Sirach 22:7 — *whoso teaches a fool is as one that glueth a potsherd together, and as he that waketh one from a sound sleep.* The futility-of-teaching-the-fool architecture; Matt 7:6's pearls-before-swine walks the same intensified into discrimination-of-audience commandment.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:7 — *Whoso teaches a fool is as one that glueth a potsherd together.* The futility of teaching the one who cannot receive; *neither cast ye your pearls before swine* (Matthew 7:6).

old: Sirach 22:8 — *he that telleth a tale to a fool speaks to one in a slumber.* The Hebrew library's don't-cast-words-on-the-unreceptive teaching; Matt 7:6 walks the same architecture as kingdom-citizens discrimination.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:8 — *He that telleth a tale to a fool speaks to one in a slumber.* Discernment of the hearer, made a kingdom rule in Matthew 7:6.

old: Sirach 22:16 — *timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* The wisdom-stream's direct foundation-architecture parallel to Matt 7:24-25's rock-foundation house that does not fall.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:16 — *so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* The hearer and doer who built on the rock (Matthew 7:24) has the heart Sirach describes.

old: Luke 6:48 -> Sirach 22:16 — *the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* Luke 6:48 names the wise builder who *digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock*; the doing is the digging-deep that stablishes the heart against the flood, the architecture the wisdom-stream named.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:16 — *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking.* Luke 6:48's builder *digged deep*, and the stream *could not shake* the house.

old: Sirach 22:17 — *a heart settled upon a thought of understanding is as a fair plaistering on the wall of a gallery.* The settled-heart architecture; Matt 7:24's hearer-and-doer settles his heart on the King's sayings.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:17 — *A heart settled upon a thought of understanding.* The settled heart is the hearer and doer of Matthew 7:24.

old: Sirach 22:18 — *pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* The inverse architecture; Matt 7:25 (against v.27's foolish-house fall) walks the same wind-against-the-foolish.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:18 — *so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* The wind of Matthew 7:25 that cannot move the house on the rock blows the pales flat.

old: Luke 6:49 -> Sirach 22:18 — *a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* Luke 6:49 names the foolish builder *without a foundation* whose house fell and *the ruin of that house was great*; the wisdom-stream named the no-foundation collapse of the unstablished heart.
new: Ecclesiasticus 22:18 — *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind.* The hearer who does not do, *without a foundation*, falls and the ruin is great (Luke 6:49).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23:9 — *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* The wisdom-counsel against the casual oath-formula apparatus; Matt 5:33-37's *swear not at all* walks the same.
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:9 — *Accustom not your mouth to swearing.* The casual oath Sirach warns against is what Matthew 5:33 begins to cut away.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23:9 — *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the accustom-not-thy-mouth-to-swearing substance — the same substance the King walks-from at Matt 5:33-37 (*swear not at all*) and walks-against at Matt 23:16 (the Pharisaic-distinction-binding-and-non-binding-oaths substance).
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:9 — *neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* Every oath counts; the graded oaths of Matthew 23:16 are the evasion Sirach's counsel never allowed.

old: Sirach 23:10 — *he that sweareth and nameth Yahuah (God) continually shall not be faultless.* The standing-consequence of habitual oath-taking; Matt 5:34's *swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is Elohim's (God's) throne* walks the same architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:10 — *he that sweareth and nameth Yahuah (God) continually shall not be faultless.* The mark habitual swearing leaves; *Swear not at all; neither by heaven* (Matthew 5:34).

old: Sirach 23:11 — *a man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house.* The cumulative-iniquity of the oath-apparatus user; Matt 5:37's *whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil* lands the same diagnostic at the heart-Torah level.
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:11 — *A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity.* The iniquity that fills the swearer is the evil Matthew 5:37 names at the root.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23:11 — *A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the man-that-useth-much-swearing-shall-be-filled-with-iniquity substance — the seriousness of every-oath the King names at Matt 23:22 (*he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sitteth thereon*).
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:11 — *and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent.* No oath is empty — to swear by heaven is to swear by the throne (Matthew 23:22).

old: Ecclesiasticus 23:19 — *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.* Ben Sira's brighter-than-the-sun eyes are the same all-hearing ear of jealousy from which murmuring is not hid in Wisdom 1:10.
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:19 — *the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun.* The eyes that see the secret parts and the ear that hears all murmuring (Wisdom of Solomon 1:10).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23:25 — *her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the no-root-and-no-fruit substance — the King walks-against at Matt 21:19's fig-tree-cursed; the architectural-substance the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 5:1-7 vineyard-substance will-walk-out at the wicked-husbandmen-parable at vv.33-46.
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:25 — *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* Leaves without fruit; the fig tree told *Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever* (Matthew 21:19).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:3 — *I came out of the mouth of the most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Wisdom-proceeding-from-the-mouth-of-the-Formless-most-High with cloud-covering-the-earth-substance; the King's *it is I* at v.27 names-himself in the same substance the wisdom-stream had identified as the Wisdom-from-the-mouth-of-the-most-High, with the cloud-rider Tanakh-substance carrying.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:3 — *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* The Word from the Father's mouth is the one on the water saying *it is I* (Matthew 14:27).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:8 — *he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* The wisdom-of-Yahuah-planted-in-Yashar'el (Israel) substance — the same vineyard-as-the-covenant-body the prophet Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 5:1-7 names the householder hires labourers into at Matt 20:1.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:8 — *Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* Wisdom planted in Yashar'el (Israel), the vineyard the householder hires labourers into (Matthew 20:1).

old: Sirach 24:9 — *He created me from the beginning before the world* Wisdom brought forth before the ages, behind *he is before all things, and by him all things consist* (Colossians 1:16-17); the Formed, not a second co-equal Elohim.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:9 — *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* Wisdom before the world is the Son by whom all things were created (Colossians 1:16).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:12 — *I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).* The wisdom-rooted-in-Yashar'el (Israel)-as-Yahuah's-inheritance substance — the natural-and-wild-olive-branches-of-the-olive-tree-of-Yashar'el (Israel) per Red Line #11; the vineyard the parable names at Matt 20:1 is the same covenant-body the wisdom-stream and the prophets named.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:12 — *I took root in an honourable people.* The honourable people is the vineyard of Matthew 20:1 — Yashar'el (Israel), the Father's own inheritance.

old: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 24:17 — *As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.* Wisdom-as-the-vine, commanded to take root in Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel) (24:8); John 15:1's *true vine* gathers the Wisdom-vine the wisdom-stream then names as the Torah (24:23).
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:17 — *As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour.* The vine of Wisdom planted in Jacob is the true vine of John 15:1.

old: Sirach 24:19 — *come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The wisdom-stream's wisdom-figure come-unto-me invitation-substance; Matt 11:19's *wisdom is justified of her children* names the body responding to the same invitation.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation; *wisdom is justified of her children* who came (Matthew 11:19).

old: Sirach 24:19 — *come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The third major wisdom-figure-come-unto-me invitation in Sirach (after chapters 6 and 51); Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour* walks the same universal-invitation-architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The same call Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*; Wisdom speaking before she came in flesh.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 — *come unto me, all ye that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-feeding-her-children invitation; the King's come-unto-me invitation across his ministry (Matt 11:28) is the operative-form, with the Matt 14:20 *they did all eat, and were filled* enacting the substance at the Galilee-desert-place.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* In the desert place *they did all eat, and were filled* (Matthew 14:20); Wisdom feeding her children, with twelve baskets left for the twelve tribes.

old: ★ *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits* (Sirach 24:19) — Wisdom's invitation parallels *come ye, buy, and eat* (Isaiah 55:1); the same come-and-be-filled call.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation stands beside Isaiah 55:1, *come ye, buy, and eat*; the same free call to come and be filled.

old: Sirach 24:21 — *they that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* Wisdom confesses her own limit; John 4:14's *whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst ... a well of water springing up into everlasting life* is the answer the wisdom-stream waited for.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:21 — *they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* The thirst that keeps a man coming back to Wisdom; at John 4:14 that same Wisdom in flesh sets the well inside him, *a well of water springing up into everlasting life*.

old: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 24:23 — *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* The Wisdom-vine named outright as the Torah; John 15:5's *I am the vine, ye are the branches ... without me ye can do nothing* — to abide in the true vine is to abide in the Word the Father spoke.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded.* Wisdom's vine named as the Torah itself; to abide in the true vine of John 15:5 is to abide in the Word the Father spoke.

old: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage* (Sirach 24:23) — the Wisdom sweeter than honey IS the Torah, the inheritance whose keeping holds *great reward* (19:11). Red Line #6 outright.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* The Wisdom sweeter than honey is the Torah, the inheritance whose keeping holds *great reward* (Psalm 19:11).

old: *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob* (Sirach 24:23) — Wisdom named as the Torah, the heritage of Jacob; the inheritance of 147:19, Red Line #6 plainly.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* Wisdom named as the Torah, the heritage of Jacob; the word, statutes and judgments shown to Yashar'el (Israel) at Psalm 147:19.

old: *he that seeks for abundance will turn his eyes away* (Ecclesiasticus 27:1) — the self-blinding of Ephraim's boast. [extras]
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:1 — *he that seeks for abundance will turn his eyes away.* The blindness of Ephraim's boast at Hosea 12:8, *they shall find none iniquity in me*; the pursuit of gain hides the sin from the sinner.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:4 — *as when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.* The post-harvest-sifting architecture — the substantial-evil-servant at Matt 24:51 walks-the-judgment-substance the prophet-Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) walked at Ezekiel 18:24 (*when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness... all his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned*); the substantial-presumption-of-the-substantial-stewardship walks-through the sieve.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:4 — *As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains.* The sifting of the household: the trusted servant's talk and conduct show what he is, and at Matthew 24:51 he is *cut asunder* and given *his portion with the hypocrites*.

old: Sirach 27:6 — *the fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The Hebrew library's direct fruit-as-utterance-of-the-heart architecture; Matt 7:16's *by their fruits ye shall know them* walks the same.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* The fruit shows the tree, the speech shows the heart; the same test Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 7:16, *ye shall know them by their fruits*.

old: Sirach 27:6 — *the fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for Matt 12:33-35's tree-by-fruit / out-of-the-abundance-of-the-heart architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Words as the fruit of the heart; *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matthew 12:34).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:6 — *the fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the tree-and-fruit-and-utterance architecture — the heart's-conceit manifests in the utterance-of-the-mouth, the same architecture the King's Matt 7:17-20 and Matt 15:18 walk.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The heart's conceit comes out in the mouth; *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart* (Matthew 15:18).

old: Luke 6:43 -> Sirach 27:6 — *the fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The Lukan good-tree / corrupt-tree teaching ties the fruit-diagnostic to the heart-utterance; the wisdom-stream named the same architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* Good tree, good fruit; corrupt tree, corrupt fruit (Luke 6:43), and the mouth is the heart's fruit.

old: Sirach 27:7 — *praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* The Hebrew library's testing-by-speaking diagnostic; Matt 7:20's *by their fruits ye shall know them* walks the same at the leadership-level.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak.* The man is tried in his speaking; *by their fruits ye shall know them* (Matthew 7:20), and a teacher's teaching is his fruit.

old: Sirach 27:7 — *praise no man before thou hearest him speak; for this is the trial of men.* The wisdom-stream's speech-as-trial-of-men architecture; the day-of-judgment at Matt 12:36 is the cosmic-version.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Speech as the trial of a man; at Matthew 12:36 that trial reaches the day of judgment, where *every idle word* is given account of.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:14 — *The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the talk-of-him-that-sweareth-much substance — the brawls-substance the wisdom-stream warns against; the Pharisaic-distinction-binding-the-oath-on-the-gift-but-not-on-the-altar at Matt 23:18 walks the same substance the wisdom-stream names against.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:14 — *The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright.* The much swearing Sirach warns of; at Matthew 23:18 it is a whole system of oaths by the altar and oaths by the gift, binding and not binding.

old: Sirach 27:30 — *malice and wrath, even these are abominations.* The heart-condition Matt 7:1-2's just-judgment teaching presupposes be cleared first; the wisdom-stream names the diagnostic.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:30 — *Malice and wrath, even these are abominations.* The heart condition that has to go before a brother is weighed; *judge not, that ye be not judged* (Matthew 7:1).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:30 — *Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the disposition-the-King-is-forming-against at Kefa (Peter)'s Matt 18:21 question — the disciple still-counting-the-offences (*till seven times?*) is still operating within the substance the wisdom-stream had named as abomination; the King's answer presses-past-the-counting into the disposition-of-no-malice the fruits-of-the-Spirit substance (Galatians 5:22-23) the new-heart of Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27 forms-the-walker-into.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:30 — *even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* Malice and wrath as the sinful man's portion; Peter's *till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21) is still counting, and the King's answer leaves the count behind.

old: Sirach 28:1 — *he that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God).* The Hebrew library's explicit measure-for-measure architecture; Matt 7:2's *with what measure ye mete* walks the same.
new: Ecclesiasticus 28:1 — *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God).* Measure for measure: *with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again* (Matthew 7:2).

old: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God)* (Ecclesiasticus 28:1) — Sirach's sage warns the avenger is overtaken by his own vengeance; the snare Abigail spares David.
new: Ecclesiasticus 28:1 — *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God).* The snare Abigail turned David from at 1 Samuel 25:26, *avenging thyself with thine own hand*.

old: Sirach 28:2 — *forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* The Hebrew library's explicit conditional-forgiveness in the wisdom-stream; Matt 6:12's *forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors* walks the same architecture in the Lord's Prayer.
new: Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* Forgiveness asked for and forgiveness given in one prayer; *forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors* (Matthew 6:12).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the conditional-forgiveness-architecture the King names at Matt 18:22 and parable-extends at vv.23-35; the same conditional-substance the King had named at Matt 6:14-15 the Lord's-Prayer's forgiveness-petition. The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly; the King institutionalizes it; the architecture is mercy-met-with-mercy at every register the wisdom-stream-and-the-King-and-the-apostles articulate.
new: Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you.* The one line behind the King's *seventy times seven* (Matthew 18:22) and the parable that follows it: forgive, and be forgiven.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:2 — *forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* The wisdom-stream articulation of the forgive-your-neighbor substance — the same substance the King walks at Matt 6:14-15 and the unforgiving-servant parable at Matt 18:23-35; the love-of-the-neighbor at Matt 22:39 walks the substance-of-forgiveness.
new: Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you.* Forgiving the hurt is love of neighbour in practice; *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself* (Matthew 22:39) begins in Leviticus 19:18 with no vengeance and no grudge.
