new: Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *have mercy upon the people that is called by your name.* Mercy remembered toward his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in Luke 1:54.

old: Sirach 36:12 — *have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* The object of the gathering — the firstborn-people called by the Name; Luke 19:10's lost-that-must-be-sought is this firstborn scattered Lo-Ammi.
new: Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *whom you have named your firstborn.* The lost whom the Son of Adam seeks (Luke 19:10) is the firstborn scattered.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:14 — *fill Sion (Zion) with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory.* The wisdom-stream's prayer-for-the-glory-to-fill-Tsion the King's-arriving-at-the-city walks-out at Matt 21:9-10. The Greek *eseisthē* the Matthean account uses for *all the city was moved* carries the same root the Matt 27:51 crucifixion-earthquake and the Matt 28:2 resurrection-earthquake carry — the wisdom-stream had-named the Father's-glory-arriving-at-Tsion as the substance-that-fills-Tsion; the gospel walks the same substance at the King-arriving-into-the-shaken-city.
new: Ecclesiasticus 36:14 — *Fill Sion with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory.* The glory entered the city at Matthew 21:9 to the cry of Hosanna.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 37:2 — *is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?* The substantial-grief-to-death substance — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel)'s *Friend, wherefore art thou come?* at Matt 26:50 + the King's *my soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death* at v.38 walks the substantial-Suffering-Servant-grief Isaiah 53:3 walks-into. The substantial-Psalm 41:9 substance the King cites at John 13:18 (*mine own familiar friend ... hath lifted up his heel against me*) walks-substantively at the same substance.
new: Ecclesiasticus 37:2 — *when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy.* *Friend, wherefore art thou come?* (Matthew 26:50) is this grief spoken in the garden.

old: Sirach 38:9 — *in your sickness ... pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The wisdom-stream's prayer-first architecture; the bleeding woman at Matt 9:20 bypasses the prescribed-mediator-chain because the King IS the direct-source the wisdom-stream's prescription pointed toward.
new: Ecclesiasticus 38:9 — *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The woman who touched the hem (Matthew 9:20) made that prayer with her hand.

old: Sirach 38:12 — *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him.* The wisdom-stream's give-place-to-the-physician prescription; the bleeding woman had given place to physicians for twelve years (Mark 5:26 records the Sirach-38 prescription faithfully followed and failed); the King's direct-touch at Matt 9:22 makes whole what the physician-chain could not.
new: Ecclesiasticus 38:12 — *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him.* The bleeding woman gave place to physicians for twelve years; at Matthew 9:22 she reached past them to the one who made them, and her faith made her whole.

old: Sirach 38:14 — *they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.* The physician's prosper-the-remedy authority depends on the Most High; at Matt 9:25 the King takes the dead girl's hand and exercises the prosper-the-remedy authority directly — the Formed-in-flesh IS the source the physician-chain prays to.
new: Ecclesiasticus 38:14 — *they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give.* The physician prays that his remedy would prosper; at Matthew 9:25 the one he prays to takes the dead girl by the hand himself.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 39:6 — *when the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the spirit-of-understanding-poured-out-on-the-elect-scribe; Matt 13:16-17's blessed-eyes-and-blessed-ears substance carries the same architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 39:6 — *he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences.* Understanding is given when Yahuah (God) wills; the blessed eyes and ears of Matthew 13:16 are given the same way.

old: Job 14:1 — *Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.* Job states the same travail-from-the-womb that Sirach 40:1 lays on every son of Adam.
new: Ecclesiasticus 40:1 — *an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb.* Job 14:1 says the same of the man born of a woman: few days, full of trouble, the yoke laid on Adam carried down his line.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:23 — *by his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands therein.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Creator's-counsel-appeasing-the-deep architecture; the Tanakh-direct-substance of Iyov (Job) 9:8 (*treadeth upon the waves of the sea*) names the action, Sirach 43:23 names the authority-behind-the-action, the King at Matt 14:25 enacts both at once.
new: Ecclesiasticus 43:23 — *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* The one who stills the deep by his counsel walks on it at Matthew 14:25; Job 9:8 said he alone treads upon the waves of the sea.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:25 — *for in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wonders-of-the-sea as the Creator's-domain; the King at Matt 14:25 walks the sea AS the Creator-of-the-sea, with the *egō eimi* of v.27 naming the speaker as the One whose-counsel-appeases-the-deep.
new: Ecclesiasticus 43:25 — *in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* The sea is the Creator's storehouse of wonders; at Matthew 14:25 the Creator walks on it and tells them, it is I.

old: Hebrews 11:1 — *Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.* The faith Hebrews defines is the very glory by which the fathers of Sirach 44:7 were honoured in their generations.
new: Ecclesiasticus 44:7 — *All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.* The honoured men of Sirach 44 are the roll of Hebrews 11; the glory of their times was faith in things not yet seen.

old: Hebrews 11:7 — *By faith Noah, being warned of Elohim (God) of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.* Hebrews makes Noah's exchange-for-the-world (Sirach 44:17) an act of saving faith.
new: Ecclesiasticus 44:17 — *Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world.* Hebrews 11:7 shows the faith behind the righteousness: Noah believed what was not yet seen and built, and was left as a remnant.

old: Genesis 17:1 — *And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* The walk-before-me-and-be-perfect of this covenant chapter is the law of the Most High Abraham kept in Sirach 44:20.
new: Ecclesiasticus 44:20 — *Who kept the law of the Most High, and was in covenant with him.* The law Abraham kept is the walk Yahuah (God) commanded at Genesis 17:1, and the covenant in his flesh is the circumcision of the same chapter.

old: Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* The Hebrew library names Eliyahu (Elijah) by the prophet-as-fire register Yochanan (John) walks at Matt 3:1.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* John comes preaching in the wilderness at Matthew 3:1 with the same fire in his word; he is the Elijah who was to come.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:1 — *then stood up Eliyahu (Elias) the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-fiery-zeal-at-the-royal-court architecture Yochanan (John)'s Torah-confrontation of Herod-Antipas at Matt 14:3-4 enacts.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *his word burned like a lamp.* Elijah's fire at Ahab's court is John's word to Herod at Matthew 14:3–4; the king answers the prophet by binding him.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:2 — *who brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern judgment-on-the-Torah-violating-court substance; Yochanan (John)'s confrontation of Herod-Antipas's Torah-violation operates in the same architecture (the famine-judgment at 1 Melakhim (Kings) 17:1 parallels the imprisonment-and-eventual-martyrdom at Matt 14:3-12).
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:2 — *by his zeal he diminished their number.* Elijah's zeal against Ahab's court brought famine; John's zeal against Herod's court brought his imprisonment at Matthew 14:3.

old: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* The Hebrew library reads the Eliyahu (Elijah)-pattern as carrying the ingathering of all twelve tribes — explicit echo of Malachi 4:5-6.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* The Elijah errand ends in the restoring of the tribes of Jacob; the voice in the wilderness at Matthew 3:3 is its beginning.

old: Sirach 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob* — the second-Temple reading of Elijah: the two-house gathering.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* The Elijah errand ends in the restoring of the tribes of Jacob; the voice in the wilderness at Matthew 3:3 is its beginning.

old: Sirach 48:10 — *ordained for reproofs in their times ... to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Eliyahu-pattern with the twelve-tribe-gathering substance (Red Line #11) integrated; Matt 11:14 names the inaugural-fulfillment in Yochanan (John).
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elias at Matthew 11:14, and Sirach says what Elijah comes to do: restore the tribes of Jacob, all twelve.

old: Sirach 48:10 — *to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Ben Sira read the Elijah-mission as the two-house restoration, centuries before John.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elias at Matthew 11:14, and Sirach says what Elijah comes to do: restore the tribes of Jacob, all twelve.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:10 — *who wast ordained for reproofs in their times ... and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob).* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Malakhi (Malachi) 4:5-6 Eliyahu-promised-return substance; the Matt 11:14 identification of Yochanan (John) as the first-Eliyahu-coming preparing-for-the-King operates in the architecture Sirach 48:10 had named. The restoration-of-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) is the framework's scattered-seed-gathering substance the wisdom-stream knew at the Eliyahu-pattern register.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God).* The multitude at Matthew 14:5 counted John a prophet; Sirach describes which prophet, the Elijah ordained for reproofs and the restoring of Jacob.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:11 — *blessed are they that saw thee, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-disciples-blessed-in-the-prophet's-departure substance; Yochanan (John)'s-disciples honor the architecture at Matt 14:12 (the burial-after-the-beheading and the going-to-tell-Yahusha (Jesus)) — the disciples drawn-into-the-King's-orbit as the operative-form of the architecture.
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:11 — *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* John's disciples at Matthew 14:12 bury the Elijah of their day and go to Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom we shall surely live.

old: Ecclesiasticus 48:12 — *Eliseus was filled with his spirit.* The Eliyahu (Elijah) / Elisha mantle-transfer-by-spirit at the Yarden (Jordan); the same river Matt 3:13 places Yahusha (Jesus) coming to Yochanan (John).
new: Ecclesiasticus 48:12 — *Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit.* The spirit passed from Elijah to Elisha at the Jordan; at Matthew 3:13 Yahusha (Jesus) comes to the same river and the Spirit descends.

old: Hebrews 9:12 — *Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.* The poured-out cup of Simon's offering (Sirach 50:15) is the shadow whose substance is the Messiah entering once with His own blood — the type, not the fulfilment.
new: Ecclesiasticus 50:15 — *poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour.* The blood of the grape at the altar's foot pictures what Hebrews 9:12 says the Messiah (Christ) did with his own blood, once.

old: Sirach 51:23 — *draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* The wisdom-stream wisdom-figure's come-unto-me invitation-substance; the typological-anchor of Matt 11:28's King's invitation to the labour-and-heavy-laden.
new: Ecclesiasticus 51:23 — *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach's closing invitation is the one Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28; come near, and find the rest in the house of learning.

old: Sirach 51:26 — *put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:29's *take my yoke upon you, and learn of me*; the framework's exchange-the-Pharisaic-burden-yoke-for-the-King's-rest-yoke reading anchored here.
new: Ecclesiasticus 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* The yoke is the instruction and the rest is found under it, not away from it; Matthew 11:29 says take my yoke, learn of me.

old: Sirach 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction... I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest* (51:27). Ben Sira: the yoke IS the instruction (the Torah/Wisdom), and rest is the fruit of bearing it — not of casting it off. The direct witness behind *take my yoke.*
new: Ecclesiasticus 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* The yoke is the instruction and the rest is found under it, not away from it; Matthew 11:29 says take my yoke, learn of me.

old: Sirach 51:27 — *behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:30's *for my yoke is easy, and my burden is light*; the wisdom-stream wisdom-yoke and the King's heart-Torah-yoke are the same yoke-substance.
new: Ecclesiasticus 51:27 — *I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach's little labour and much rest under the yoke is Matthew 11:30, my yoke is easy and my burden is light.

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:30 — *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* THE direct verbal-anchor for the work-your-work-betimes + reward-in-his-time substance; the substantial-reward the faithful-servants walk-into at Matt 25:23's *enter thou into the joy of thy lord* is the substantial-millennial-reign-stewardship per Revelation 2:26-27, 3:21, 5:10, 20:4-6 + the twelve-thrones at Matt 19:28.
new: Ecclesiasticus 51:30 — *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* The reward comes in his time; at Matthew 25:23 the faithful servant receives it when the master returns, not before.

old: Daniel 11:30 — *For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.* the same tyrant-against-the-covenant pattern Judith 4:7 braces for at the passes into Judea.
new: Judith 4:7 — *it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was straight.* The invader Judith's people brace for at the passes is the king of Daniel 11:30, whose indignation is against the holy covenant.

old: Judith 9:11 — *For your power stands not in multitude nor your might in strong men: for you are a Yahuah (God) of the afflicted, an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.* Judith confesses the very Helper-of-the-forlorn that Esther leans on, two women with no help but Him.
new: Judith 9:11 — *a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.* Esther prays the same thing at The Rest of Esther 14:14, no other help but you; two women alone before a power bent on their people.

old: 1 Corinthians 1:27 — *But Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;* Yahuah disappointing a vast army by the hand of one widow (Judith 16:6) is the very weak-confound-the-mighty principle Paul preaches.
new: Judith 16:6 — *the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.* Yahuah (God) bringing an army to nothing by the hand of a widow is the weak confounding the mighty of 1 Corinthians 1:27.

old: Psalm 148:5 — *Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.* Judith 16:14 ('you spakest, and they were made') confesses the same creation-by-the-word for which Psalm 148 calls all creatures to praise.
new: Judith 16:14 — *for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them.* Creation by the spoken word; Psalm 148:5 calls all of it to praise the one who commanded, and they were created.

old: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* Israel taken 'from among all people' is Moses' chosen-above-all-people, the ground of Esther's confidence.
new: The Rest of Esther 14:5 — *tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance.* Esther in exile recites what Moses said at Deuteronomy 7:6, a people chosen from among all people, and the choosing holds in the scattering.

old: Leviticus 26:41 — *And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:* The Torah foretold the giving-into-enemy-hands and the humbled heart that turns it back, the frame Esther prays inside.
new: The Rest of Esther 14:6 — *we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies.* Esther prays inside Leviticus 26:41, the sin named, the enemy's hand owned as just, the humbled heart that turns the curse toward home.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wisdom-shall-not-enter-the-malicious-soul architecture; the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 6:9-10 hardening-citation at Matt 13:13-15 names the operative-form.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter.* Wisdom does not enter a soul set against her; at Matthew 13:13 the parables meet eyes that have closed themselves.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* The wisdom-stream's no-word-goes-for-nought-and-the-mouth-that-belieth-slays-the-soul architecture; the day-of-judgment substance of Matt 12:36-37.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought.* No word goes for nothing; Matthew 12:36 says every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting ... the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the mouth-and-tongue-substance overlap with the King's-Matt-15:19-catalogue (murmuring, backbiting, the lying-mouth as soul-slaying substance; false witness, blasphemies as the King's-catalogue substance).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* The lying mouth of Wisdom 1:11 and the false witness of Matthew 15:19 come from the same place, the heart.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 — *Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* The wisdom-stream's articulation that the Father is-not-the-source of the death-and-the-grave; the gates-of-Sheol do not have-permanence-against the assembly the King builds because the gates do not originate-with-the-Father.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 — *Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* Death is not of Yahuah's (God's) making, so the gates of the grave at Matthew 16:18 have no lasting claim on the assembly he builds.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous ... he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The Hebrew library's just-man-as-rebuke-to-the-lawless register; the wider backdrop to Matt 8:17's Isaiah 53:4 Servant-credential.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn.* The righteous one of Wisdom 2 is Isaiah's servant; at Matthew 8:17 he bears our sicknesses while the ungodly lie in wait for him.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous ... he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The wisdom-stream's direct prophecy of the system's-rejection-of-the-righteous-one; Matt 11:18-19's children-in-marketplaces names the operative-form at the apostolic-mission level.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The contradictory complaints of Matthew 11:19 hide the real grievance Wisdom 2:12 names: the righteous one reproves their lawbreaking.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the ungodly-determining-to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous architecture; Yochanan (John) upbraided Herod with the Torah-violation, Herod-Herodias determined to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous, the architecture matches the wisdom-stream's naming centuries before.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* John upbraids Herod with the law at Matthew 14:3–4 and is bound for it, the ungodly lying in wait for the righteous.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the wicked's-plot-against-the-righteous-one substance — the elders-and-chief-priests-and-scribes of Matt 16:21 enact the operative-form the wisdom-stream had named at the prefiguring-passage centuries before.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The plot of Wisdom 2 ends in a shameful death; at Matthew 16:21 Yahusha (Jesus) names the same end and adds the third day.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn ... he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The lying-in-wait of the ungodly against the just man who reproves them; John 18:3's band of men and officers walks the same arrest of the righteous one.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The band with lanterns and torches at John 18:3 is the lying in wait of the ungodly for the righteous one who reproves them.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calleth himself the child of Yahuah (the Lord).* The ungodly identify the righteous-one by his Sonship-claim; Matt 4:3's *if thou be the Son of Elohim (God)* enacts the same testing-by-challenge.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The ungodly test the righteous one's claim to be the child of Yahuah (God); the tempter at Matthew 4:3 says if thou be the Son.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calleth himself the child of Yahuah (the Lord) ... his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion.* The wisdom-stream's child-of-Elohim-by-righteous-disposition architecture; Matt 12:50's kingdom-family-recognition criterion walks the same substance.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life of another fashion; Matthew 12:50 says the same, whoever does the will of my Father.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The exact charge of John 19:7 — *he made himself the Son of Elohim (God)* — the self-designation the ungodly treat as the capital offence.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The capital charge of John 19:7, he made himself the Son of Elohim (God), is the complaint Wisdom 2:13 gives the ungodly.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion.* The aesthetic-rejection of the righteous-one the wisdom-stream named; Matt 11:19's *gluttonous-man, winebibber, friend-of-publicans-and-sinners* slander is the operative-form.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* The life of another fashion is what the slander of Matthew 11:19 was aimed at — a glutton and winebibber for sitting with sinners.

old: Wisdom 2:16 — *he maketh his boast that Elohim (God) is his father.* The ungodly's resentment of the Sonship-boast; Matt 4:6's testing-of-the-claimed-Sonship dynamic walks the same.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* The boast the ungodly resent is the claim the tempter dares him to prove at Matthew 4:6.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *we are esteemed of him as counterfeits ... he maketh his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the wicked's-grievance against the righteous-one's-credentialing — the Pharisaic-and-Sadducean-second-Temple-aristocracy reads the King's-very-existence as the indictment-of-their-counterfeit-credentialing, the architecture the wisdom-stream had named.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness.* The grievance of the religious seat, which is why he must suffer of the elders and chief priests and scribes (Matthew 16:21).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *he makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* The righteous one is grievous to the ungodly because he claims the Father as his own; John 18:38's Pilate finds *no fault at all,* yet the chief priests press for death on exactly this ground.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* Pilate found no fault at all (John 18:38); the only charge was the one Wisdom named.

old: Wisdom 2:18 — *if the just man be the Son of Elohim (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The direct prefiguring of Matt 4:6 — the *let-Elohim-save-him-if-he-is-his* taunt; the devil's cut-quote of Psalm 91 is the *let-the-angels-save-him* instance of the Wisdom architecture.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly's test is the devil's dare at Matthew 4:6, down to the cut quotation of Psalm 91.

old: Wisdom 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The just-man-as-son-of-Yahuah architecture; Matt 8:17's Servant who bears the people's infirmities walks the same.

new: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God).* The man without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:12) has no crown to receive; the kingdom and the crown go to those clothed for the feast.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* The glorious-kingdom + beautiful-crown + Father's-right-hand-covering substance — the inheritance-of-the-resurrected-righteous the wisdom-stream had named the architecture for. Ties forward to v.18's *all power is given unto me in heaven and in earth* — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) seated at the Father's right-hand walks the operative-form.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them.* The risen King the women worshipped (Matthew 28:9) is the first of the righteous to receive the kingdom and the crown from the Father's hand.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:4 — *because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God).* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the ministers-of-the-kingdom-have-not-judged-aright-nor-kept-the-law substance — the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the contrary-to-Torah-test the framework applies-against any system claiming covenant-standing while teaching contrary-to-the-Torah-substance. Matt 23:13's leadership-substance shuts-up-the-kingdom by walking the very-substance Wisdom of Solomon 6:4 names.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:4 — *being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law.* Ministers who have not kept the law are the ones who shut up the kingdom against men (Matthew 23:13).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* The wisdom-stream's graduated-accountability-by-credentialing principle; Matt 11:21-22 names the operative-application to the Galilean-cities-of-the-credentialing.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Chorazin and Bethsaida (Matthew 11:21) saw the mighty works and did not repent; the more shown, the sharper the judgment.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* The wisdom-stream's direct statement of graduated-accountability; Matt 11:22's *more tolerable for Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon)* names the operative-application.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* More tolerable for Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:22): the judgment is real and weighed by what each was shown.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* The wisdom-stream's sore-trial-upon-the-mighty; Matt 11:23's Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum) is the *exalted-unto-heaven* mighty under the sore-trial.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Capernaum, exalted unto heaven and brought down to the grave (Matthew 11:23), is the mighty under the sore trial.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *wisdom is glorious ... easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* The Hebrew library's direct seekers-find architecture; Matt 7:7's *seek, and ye shall find* walks the same.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* Seek and ye shall find (Matthew 7:7) is the promise Solomon wrote about wisdom first.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *found of such as seek her.* The rhythm of ask-seek-knock.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* Seek and ye shall find (Matthew 7:7) is the promise Solomon wrote about wisdom first.

old: Wisdom 6:13 — *she preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known to them.* The Father-runs-to-meet architecture; Matt 7:7's threefold ask/seek/knock walks the same reciprocation.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:13 — *She preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known to them.* Wisdom goes before those who desire her; the Father answers ask, seek, knock (Matthew 7:7) because he came out to meet the seeker first.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:18 — *love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the love-is-the-keeping-of-her-laws substance — the same substance the apostle Yochanan (John) names explicitly at 1 John 5:2-3 (*this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous*); the heart-Torah-architecture the King walks at Matt 22:40.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:18 — *love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption.* The two commandments all the law hangs on (Matthew 22:40) do not replace the law; love is the keeping of it.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you; but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light.* The wisdom-stream's commitment-to-reveal-the-mysteries operates in the same register the King's parables-method enacts.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you.* Things kept secret from the foundation of the world uttered in parables (Matthew 13:35) is the same refusal to hide mysteries.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* The wisdom-stream's prayer-channel for the Spirit-of-wisdom; Matt 11:25-27's Father-Son revelation-economy operates through the King's prayer.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Understanding is given to the one who prays; the Father reveals to babes what the wise cannot reach (Matthew 11:25).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her ... all gold in respect of her is as a little sand.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the wisdom-preferred-above-all-else; the buyer (per the framework's preferred Father-Son-buyer reading) prefers-the-pearl-above-all-else and pays-the-full-price-to-obtain.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* The merchant who sells all for one pearl (Matthew 13:45) is doing Solomon's arithmetic: sceptres and riches are nothing beside wisdom.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure unto men that never faileth.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the never-failing-treasure substance; the treasure-hid-in-the-field at Matt 13:44 carries the same supreme-worth at the kingdom-of-heaven register.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God).* The treasure hid in a field worth selling all for (Matthew 13:44) is the treasure that never fails and makes friends of Yahuah (God).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* what flows out from the glory without diminishing it, named in a person at Hebrews 1:3.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* What flows out from the glory without lessening it is a person in Hebrews 1:3, the brightness of his glory.

old: Wisdom 7:25 — *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God)... flowing from the glory of the Almighty* derived glory, brought forth from the One; the Formed *in the form of Elohim (God)* (Philippians 2:6).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* The breath of the power flowing from the glory is the one in the form of Elohim (God) (Philippians 2:6), brought forth, not a rival.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *O Elohim (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (Lord) of mercy, who hast made all things with thy word.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Word-as-the-Father's-agent-of-creation architecture; the King at Matt 14:25-27 walks-on-the-sea (the creation-substance) AS the Word-through-whom-all-things-were-made (Yochanan (John) 1:3) — one architecture: the Father's-Word who made-all-things + the Word-was-made-flesh + the King-walking-on-the-sea-and-naming-himself-Ehyeh.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* The Word all things were made with walks on the sea and says it is I (Matthew 14:27).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word.* The wisdom-stream articulation of the made-all-things-with-thy-word substance — the same substance the apostle Yochanan (John) walks at John 1:1-3; the substance-the-Father-claims at Matt 22:21 is the substance-the-Father-made-with-his-Word (the Formed-Expression through-whom-all-things-were-made).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* Render unto Elohim (God) the things that are his (Matthew 22:21): all things, since he made them all with his word.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and ... a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* The wisdom-stream's enduring-monument-to-judgment; Matt 11:24's *more tolerable for the land of Sodom* invokes the abiding-witness as the floor against which the credentialed-cities are weighed.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Sodom, the standing monument of unbelief, is the floor the King measures Capernaum against (Matthew 11:24).

old: *brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him... gave him perpetual glory* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:14) — the exaltation of 105:21-22: not left in bonds but raised to the sceptre.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 10:14 — *left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom.* Joseph, not left in bonds but made lord of Pharaoh's house (Psalm 105:21), is the sold man raised to the sceptre.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The wisdom-stream's cogitation-that-would-never-be-changed architecture; the blasphemy's hardened-disposition is the operative-form.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The cogitation that would never be changed is the heart behind the word against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) that is not forgiven (Matthew 12:32).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 12:19 — *by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful, and have made your children to be of a good hope that you give repentance for sins.* The Father's mercy-pattern as the teaching-source of the just-man-should-be-merciful ethic; Matt 5:44-45's *that ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven* walks the same Father-pattern.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 12:19 — *by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful.* Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44) is the lesson the Father taught by his own mercy on enemies.

old: Wisdom 12:20 — *you did punish the enemies of your children, and the condemned to death, with such deliberation, giving them time and place, by which they might be delivered from their malice.* The Father's long-suffering-toward-enemies pattern; Matt 5:45's *he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good* walks the same standing-mercy architecture.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 12:20 — *giving them time and place, by which they might be delivered from their malice.* Sun on the evil and rain on the unjust (Matthew 5:45) is the time and place the Father gives enemies to turn.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The Father's direct sea-governance architecture; Matt 8:26's rebuke-of-the-winds walks the same in flesh-presence.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea.* The one who rebuked the winds and the sea (Matthew 8:26) is the one whose providence governs it.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *but thy providence, O Father, governeth it: for thou hast made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father's-providence-governing-the-sea architecture, echoing Tehillim (Psalm) 77:19; the King at Matt 14:25 walks the way the Father's-providence-makes-in-the-sea, and the King's catch-of-Kefa (Peter) at v.31 is the safe-path-in-the-waves the wisdom-stream named.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The King walking on the sea in the fourth watch (Matthew 14:25) is walking the way the Father made in the sea.

old: Wisdom 14:4 — *shewing that you can save from all danger.* The save-from-all-danger architecture; Matt 8:25's *Lord, save us: we perish* walks the same trust-grammar.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 14:4 — *Shewing that you can save from all danger.* Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25) is answered by the one who can save from all danger at sea (Matthew 8:26).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the Most High's power-over-life-and-death; Matt 9:24-25's raising of Yair (Jairus)'s daughter is the in-flesh exercise of the same authority.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The maid not dead but sleeping (Matthew 9:24) is raised by the one who leads to the grave and brings up again.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of Sheol, and bringest up again.* The wisdom-stream's gates-of-Sheol-and-bring-up-again architecture; Matt 12:40's three-days-in-the-heart-of-the-earth is the operative-application.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The sign of Jonah walks that road: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, then up (Matthew 12:40).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gates-of-hell-and-the-bringing-up-again substance. The Father's-power leads-to-the-gates-and-brings-up-again; the assembly built on the resurrected-King partakes-of-the-bringing-up-again the Father's-power has-always-held.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The gates that could not hold the raised King will not prevail against his assembly (Matthew 16:18).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 — *a man indeed killeth ... the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not.* The mortal-man-cannot-bring-back diagnostic; the King at Matt 9:25 brings back the spirit that has gone — confirming the Formed-from-the-Formless framework on the nature of Yahusha (Jesus).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 — *the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not.* What no man can do, the King does with his hand on a dead girl (Matthew 9:25).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wilderness-manna substance the King at Matt 14:19 enacts at the Galilee-desert-place; the Yochanan (John) 6 *I am the bread of life* discourse following the Yochanan-account locks the King as the bread-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour.* Bread without labour again, blessed and broken in a desert place and handed out by the disciples (Matthew 14:19).

old: Wisdom 16:20 — *...thou feddest thy own people with angels' food... bread prepared without their labour.* The library names the manna heaven's bread; here the loaves come by blessing, *looking up to heaven*.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour.* Bread without labour again, blessed and broken in a desert place and handed out by the disciples (Matthew 14:19).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *instead of which you feddest your own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste.* The manna named angels' food, heaven-sent and labourless; John 6:31's *our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat* cites the same wilderness bread.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *you feddest your own people with angels’ food.* The crowd cites the same wilderness bread, *He gave them bread from heaven to eat* (John 6:31).

old: John 6:33 — *For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* The sweetness of the heavenly sustenance in Wisdom of Solomon 16:21 finds its substance in the Bread that gives life to the world.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:21 — *your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children.* The sweetness the wilderness tasted is the Bread who comes down and gives life to the world (John 6:33).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but that it is thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.* The wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the bread-of-life-is-the-Word-of-Yahuah substance the Yochanan (John) 6:63 discourse explicitly anchors (*the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life*); the feeding-substance at Matt 14:19 points beyond-the-loaves to the Word-of-the-King.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word.* The loaves blessed and broken point past themselves to the word that nourishes (Matthew 14:19).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* The wisdom-stream's reading of the manna as a sign of the word that nourishes; John 6:32-33's *true bread from heaven ... the bread of Elohim (God) ... giveth life unto the world* lands that word on the Word made flesh.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* The word that preserved the wilderness is the true bread the Father now gives (John 6:32).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 — *thine almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction.* THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the all-powerful-Word-leaping-down-from-heaven substance; the King's *it is I* (*egō eimi*) across the dark water at the fourth-watch is the operative-form of the Word-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named at the Father's-royal-throne register.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 — *Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne.* The Word who came down on Passover night speaks across the dark water, *it is I; be not afraid* (Matthew 14:27).

old: Hebrews 4:12 — *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.* The Word-as-sharp-sword of Wisdom 18:16, now turned inward to discern the heart.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 18:16 — *brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword.* The same sword, now sharper than any twoedged sword and turned on the heart (Hebrews 4:12).

old: Tobit 4:3 — *my son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life.* The second-Temple-Yashar'el (Israel)-household's deathbed-instruction articulating the all-the-days-of-her-life parental-honor extension. The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition the King exposes at vv.5-6 voids exactly this architecture; the wisdom-stream had named the substance the tradition was voiding centuries before.
new: Tobit 4:3 — *despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life.* The commandment to honour father and mother, kept to the end of her days, which the gift tradition voided (Matthew 15:4).

old: Tobit 4:3 — *despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* The paternal-instruction-substance in Tobit-the-father's teaching of his son Tobias — the broader-context framing the Tanakh-paternal-blessing the King-enacts at Matt 19:15's laying-on-of-hands (Bereshit (Genesis) 48 + Numbers 6:24-26).
new: Tobit 4:3 — *My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother.* A father handing covenant life to his son; the King laying hands on the children brought to him (Matthew 19:15).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *give alms ... and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The wisdom-stream's alms-with-eye-not-envious architecture; Matt 9:11-13's Pharisaic indignation is the inverse: envy of the mercy extended to the marginalized in the costume of purity-credential.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, which the Pharisees at the table had forgotten (Matthew 9:13).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The give-alms + face-of-Yahuah-shall-not-be-turned-away substance — the substantial-doing walks the substantial-face-of-Yahuah-toward-the-doer; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-identification-with-his-brethren at Matt 25:40 (*done it unto me*) walks the same architecture per Acts 9:4-5's *why persecutest thou me?*
new: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The face not turned from the poor meets the King in the least of his brethren (Matthew 25:40).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The sister apocryphal wisdom-book teaches the same: alms quench sin as water quencheth fire (Ecclesiasticus 3:30).
new: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* Sirach's picture of the same mercy: *alms makes an atonement for sins* as water quenches fire (Ecclesiasticus 3:30).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* — Tobit's almsgiving charge, the apocryphal sibling to Sirach 7:32's hand stretched to the poor.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor.* Sirach adds the hand to the face: *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The same restored-library wisdom: give without the envious eye that blemishes the deed in Sirach 18:15.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *when you give alms, let not your eye be envious.* Sirach's twin warning, not to blemish the good deed with uncomfortable words (Ecclesiasticus 18:15).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The charity-tithe given 'to them to whom it was meet' in Tobit 1:8 is the same alms-righteousness Tobit later commands his son.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The charge to his son is the third tithe Tobit himself paid from his orphan years (Tobit 1:8).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The alms his wife throws in his face are the very practice Tobit will charge upon his son as the way of righteousness.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The alms Anna threw in his face are the alms he charges on his son (Tobit 2:14).

old: Luke 11:41 — *But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.* Yahusha makes almsgiving the inward cleansing — exactly Tobit's 'give of thy substance' that keeps Yahuah's face turned toward the giver.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The alms that make all things clean (Luke 11:41) are the alms Tobit charged on his son.

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The restored Tobit names the almsgiving for the poor that the temple treasury safeguarded in 2-maccabees 3:10.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor.* The temple treasury kept money for widows and the fatherless, the same alms held in public trust (2 Maccabees 3:10).

old: Tobit 4:7-8 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor... be not afraid to give according to that little* give without a grudging eye, of abundance or of little; *not grudgingly, or of necessity* (2 Corinthians 9:7).
new: Tobit 4:7 — *when you give alms, let not your eye be envious.* Give of abundance or of little, without the envious eye; *not grudgingly, or of necessity* (2 Corinthians 9:7).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *when you give alms... turn not your face from any poor* the open-handed care Paul orders the believing household to extend to its widows (1 Timothy 5:16).
new: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor.* The household relieves its own widows first (1 Timothy 5:16), the face never turned from the nearest poor.

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance... turn not your face from any poor* the neighbour-serving good work behind *let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful* (Titus 3:14).
new: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The good work for necessary uses that keeps the believer from being unfruitful (Titus 3:14).

old: *Give alms of your substance... neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* (Tobit 4:7) — the exile-righteous Tobit lives the Mishpat of *Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him* (Exodus 22:21) among the nations.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The stranger in Nineveh keeps the mercy Torah commanded toward the stranger (Exodus 22:21).

old: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance... and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* — old Yashar'el (Israel) taught secret-handed giving.
new: Tobit 4:7 — *the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* Alms given for the Father's face, not for men's eyes (Matthew 6:1).

old: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The alms-as-laid-up-treasure architecture; the Sermon's own *treasures in heaven* (Matt 6:19-20) walks the same; Matt 9:13's Hosea-6:6 citation locks the diagnostic against the Pharisaic-counterfeit.
new: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The treasure laid up by mercy, the thing Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

old: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The wisdom-stream's laying-up-good-treasure-against-the-day substance in Tobit's almsgiving-instruction-context (Tobit 4:7-11) — the substance the King's-test of the rich-young-ruler at Matt 19:21 lands on (the substance of giving-to-the-poor as laying-up-treasure-in-heaven per Devarim (Deuteronomy) 15:7-8 + Mishlei (Proverbs) 19:17).
new: Tobit 4:9 — *a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Give to the poor and have treasure in heaven (Matthew 19:21), the treasure Tobit told his son to lay up.

old: Tobit 4:9 — *for you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The Hebrew library's *lay up treasure against the day* phrasing inside the charge to give alms; Luke 12:33's *provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not* walks the same architecture.
new: Tobit 4:9 — *a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The alms given now are the bags that wax not old, the treasure that faileth not (Luke 12:33).

old: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity* almsgiving as good works laid up; the open-handed fruit of *be careful to maintain good works* (Titus 3:8).
new: Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Alms as good works laid up, the fruit of a believing heart careful to maintain them (Titus 3:8).

old: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The protection-economy of the open hand; Matt 6:20's corruption-proof storehouse walks the same architecture.
new: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The deliverance the open hand brings, stored where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt (Matthew 6:20).

old: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The wisdom-stream's alms-as-deliverance-architecture; the mercy-substance IS the deliverance-substance.
new: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy is what delivers, and mercy is what Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

old: Tobit 4:10 — *alms doth deliver from death, and shall not suffer thee to come into darkness.* THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the mercy-as-substance-with-eternal-weight architecture.
new: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy carries eternal weight; the Sabbath condemnation showed a system that had lost it (Matthew 12:7).

old: Tobit 4:10 — *because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The protection-economy of the open hand; Luke 12:33's *a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth* walks the same protection-against-loss architecture.
new: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The open hand delivers from death; its treasure is in the heavens where no thief approacheth (Luke 12:33).

old: Tobit 4:15 — *do that to no man which thou hatest.* The Hebrew library's explicit Golden Rule in negative form, centuries before the Sermon; Matt 7:12 restores the same teaching in positive form as the heart-substance of *the law and the prophets.*
new: Tobit 4:15 — *Do that to no man which you hatest.* The golden rule in negative form, generations before *this is the law and the prophets* (Matthew 7:12).

old: Tobit 4:15 — *Do that to no man which you hatest* — the negative golden rule, generations before.
new: Tobit 4:15 — *Do that to no man which you hatest.* The golden rule in negative form, generations before *this is the law and the prophets* (Matthew 7:12).

old: Tobit 4:16 — *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms.* THE direct verbal-anchor for two of the six-fold-criterion at Matt 25:35-36, in continuity with Isaiah 58:6-10 + Job 31:16-22 + Deuteronomy 10:18-19 + Proverbs 19:17. NOT the substantial-categorical-charity-program; the substantial-mercy is toward the King's-brethren-during-the-tribulation per Red Line #7.
new: Tobit 4:16 — *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked.* Two of the King's own measures at the judgment, *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat* (Matthew 25:35).

old: Tobit 8:6 — *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.* Tobias's-prayer-at-the-marriage-bed directly invokes Bereshit (Genesis) 1-2's creation-ordinance — the wisdom-stream's direct corroboration of the Father-joins-the-one-flesh-substance the King names at Matt 19:6.
new: Tobit 8:6 — *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay.* The creation prayed over a marriage bed; *What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder* (Matthew 19:6).

old: Malachi 2:15 — *And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.* The godly-seed purpose of marriage is precisely Tobias’s not-for-lust-but-uprightly (Tobit 8:7).
new: Tobit 8:7 — *I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly.* Marriage entered uprightly, for the godly seed Malachi says it was made for (Malachi 2:15).

old: Tobit 12:8 — *prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* The wisdom-stream's prayer-fasting-alms-righteousness triad; Matt 9:14's Pharisaic-fasting-question presupposes the credential-without-the-mercy-triad operative, and the King reframes fasting in the bridegroom-architecture without abolishing it.
new: Tobit 12:8 — *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* Fasting belongs with prayer, alms, and righteousness, not alone; the King keeps it in that place (Matthew 9:14).

old: Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* The angel Raphael's closing instruction names the mercy-substance as the very forgiveness-substance the King exercises at the paralytic's pronouncement (Matt 9:2) and the Mattityahu (Matthew) table (Matt 9:13).
new: Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* Mercy with the weight of life and death, the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).

old: Tobit 13:3 — *confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.* The wisdom-stream's direct instruction; Matt 10:32's *whosoever therefore shall confess me before men* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level.
new: Tobit 13:3 — *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.* The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King confesses them before his Father (Matthew 10:32).

old: Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations.* The wisdom-stream's scourge-mercy-gathering architecture; the same gathering-mission Matt 10:6 commissions.
new: Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations.* The gathering Tobit prayed for is the mission to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 10:6).

old: Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* The wisdom-stream's articulation of the scourge-then-mercy-then-gathering-out-of-all-nations substance — the exact architecture the prophets had named (Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:21) and the King's-mission at v.24 enacts.
new: Tobit 13:5 — *will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) Yahusha (Jesus) was sent to are the scattered Tobit said would be gathered (Matthew 15:24).

old: Tobit 14:5 — *they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) gloriously.* The multi-stage gathering-architecture: FIRST post-Babylon return, THEN latter-time return from all places of the captivity. Matt 10:23's standing-mission is the present-age work between the two stages.
new: Tobit 14:5 — *afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously.* Two returns, the second still to come; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).

old: Tobit 14:6 — *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols* the turning made tangible in the collection: those gathered from the nations rendering back to the saints at Jerusalem (Romans 15:27).
new: Tobit 14:6 — *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* The collection for Jerusalem is the turning made tangible, carnal things paid back for spiritual things received (Romans 15:27).

old: Tobit 1:10 — *all my brethren … did eat of the bread of the Gentiles* the captive's case behind the weak who eateth herbs: the heathen table refused (Romans 14:2).
new: Tobit 1:10 — *all my brothers and those that were of my kindred did eat of the bread of the Gentiles* the captive's case behind the weak who eateth herbs: the heathen table refused (Romans 14:2).

old: John 1:5 — *And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.* Wisdom *found before* the light, against whom *vice shall not prevail* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:29-30), is John's Light the darkness cannot overcome.
new: John 1:5 — *And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.* Wisdom, who *being compared with the light, she is found before it*, and against whom *vice shall not prevail* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:29–30), is John's Light the darkness cannot overcome.

old: Jubilees 16:6 — *And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom. But Lot we saved; for Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow.* The now-live Jubilees self-links Wisdom's deliverance of *the righteous man* from the fire (10:6).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 10:6 — *she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.* Jubilees 16:6–7 tells the same judgment of Sodom and the saving of Lot for Abraham's sake.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 13:1 — *Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster;* the thesis that idolatry is 'the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil' (Wisdom of Solomon 14:27) completes the polemic begun in 13:1, the Creator unknown though seen — the very pairing Romans 1:20 and 1:25 draw on.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 13:1 — *Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of Yahuah (God), and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster;* the thesis that idolatry is *the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:27) completes the polemic begun in 13:1, the Creator unknown though seen — the very pairing Romans 1:20 and 1:25 draw on.

old: James 1:15 — *Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.* Yahuah gave *no man licence to sin* (Sirach 15:20); sin is born of a man's own conceived lust, not of any divine warrant.
new: James 1:15 — *Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.* *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin* (Ecclesiasticus 15:20); sin is born of a man's own conceived lust, not of any divine warrant.

old: Hebrews 5:4 — *And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of Elohim (God), as was Aaron.* — the *everlasting covenant* of priesthood Yahuah *made with him* (Sirach 45:7) is the honour Hebrews says no man may seize but must be called to, as Aaron was.
new: Hebrews 5:4 — *And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of Elohim (God), as was Aaron.* *An everlasting covenant he made with him and gave him the priesthood among the people* (Ecclesiasticus 45:7) — the priesthood is the honour Hebrews says no man may seize but must be called to, as Aaron was.

old: *was present when thou madest the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9) — *When he prepared the heavens, I was there* (8:27): the Formed Son present at the making.
new: *was present when you madest the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9) — *When he prepared the heavens, I was there* (Proverbs 8:27): the Formed Son present at the making.

old: ★ *O blessed are they which love thee, for they shall rejoice in thy peace... and shall be glad for ever* (Tobit 13:14) — Tobit, praying from captivity, sings the same blessing on Jerusalem's lovers that 122:6 pronounces.
new: ★ *O blessed are they which love you, for they shall rejoice in your peace* (Tobit 13:14) — Tobit, praying from captivity, sings the same blessing on Jerusalem's lovers that Psalm 122:6 pronounces.

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but... thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.* The Father who marks the sparrow preserves His own.
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* The Father who marks the sparrow preserves His own (Matthew 10:29).

old: Sirach 7:27-28 — *Honour thy father with thy whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of thy mother.* The fifth word is never abolished; *love me more* is an ordering of loves, not a cancelling.
new: Ecclesiasticus 7:27–28 — *Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.* The fifth word is never abolished; loving the Master more is an ordering of loves, not a cancelling (Matthew 10:37).

old: ★ *Set not your heart upon goods unjustly gotten, for they shall not profit you in the day of calamity* (Sirach 5:8) — the banquet *removed* (Amos 6:7) when the calamity comes.
new: ★ *Set not yours heart upon goods unjustly gotten, for they shall not profit you in the day of calamity* (Ecclesiasticus 5:8) — the banquet *removed* (Amos 6:7) when the calamity comes.

old: ★ *he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder* (Sirach 34:22) — to *build up Zion with blood* (Micah 3:10) is exactly this; the city raised on judges for reward and priests for hire is built of stolen lives.
new: ★ *he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22) — to *build up Zion with blood* (Micah 3:10) is exactly this; the city raised on judges for reward and priests for hire is built of stolen lives.

old: Sirach 47:17 — *The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.* The library remembers the fame that drew the nations to Solomon; yet a greater than Solomon is here.
new: Ecclesiasticus 47:17 — *The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.* The library remembers the fame that drew the nations to Solomon; yet a greater than Solomon is here (Luke 11:31).

old: ★ *thou gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:3) — the restored witness to the *fire by night* that led the son (Deuteronomy 1:33).
new: ★ *you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:3) — the restored witness to the *fire by night* that led the son (Deuteronomy 1:33).

old: *Be as a father to the fatherless... so shalt thou be as the son of the Most High.* (Sirach 4:10) — the wisdom tradition names Job's deed as the mark of a true son.
new: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:10) — the wisdom tradition names Job's deed as the mark of a true son (Job 29:16).

old: Prayer of Manasseh 1:11-14 (apocrypha) — the very prayer attributed to him: *I bow the knee of my heart... for you are Yahuah (God) of them that repent*.
new: Prayer of Manasseh 1:11 — *Now therefore I bow the knee of my heart, beseeching you of grace.* The very prayer attributed to him, the inside of the humbling by which Yahuah (God) was intreated (2 Chronicles 33:13).

old: 2 Esdras 7:32 — *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed unto them.* The wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the earth-shall-restore-those-that-are-asleep substance — the prophet Daniel's Daniel 12:2 substance carried-forward at the apocalyptic-wisdom-stream-register; the asleep-awaiting-the-resurrection substance the framework reads, NOT the inherited-Christian immediate-disembodied-soul substance.
new: 2 Esdras 7:32 — *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence.* The dead sleep and wait for the earth to give them back, the resurrection Yahusha (Jesus) defends against the Sadducees (Matthew 22:31).

old: Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:9 (with 24:3, *I came out of the mouth of the Most High*) — *he created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* Wisdom's own from-eternity testimony, created before the world and dwelling in Ya'aqov (Jacob) and Yashar'el (Israel); John 8:58's *Before Abraham was, I am* names the same eternity in the Formed Word who came to tabernacle among his own.
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:9 — *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* Wisdom's own testimony from before the world, dwelling in Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel); *Before Abraham was, I am* (John 8:58) names the same eternity in the Formed Word who came to tabernacle among his own.

old: 2 Esdras 3:7 — death *appointed in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people … out of number* the reign of death from Adam over all his seed (Romans 5:14).
new: 2 Esdras 3:7 — *immediately you appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.* The reign of death from Adam over all his seed (Romans 5:14).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 2:21 — *they were deceived: for their own wickedness has blinded them* the root of the world's false wisdom, which *Elohim (God) hath made foolish* (1 Corinthians 1:20).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 2:21 — *and were deceived: for their own wickedness has blinded them.* The root of the false wisdom Elohim (God) *made foolish* (1 Corinthians 1:20).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 — *their hope is full of immortality,* the reward of the righteous the ungodly *neither hoped... nor discerned* (Wisdom 2:22); the unseen *things which Elohim (God) hath prepared for them that love him* (1 Corinthians 2:9).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 — *yet is their hope full of immortality.* The reward of the righteous the ungodly neither hoped for nor discerned (Wisdom of Solomon 2:22); the unseen *things which Elohim (God) hath prepared for them that love him* (1 Corinthians 2:9).

old: 2 Esdras 7:29 — *my son Messiah (Christ) [shall] die, and all men that have life* the library's universal death, then the raising; *as in Adam all die, even so in Messiah all made alive* (1 Corinthians 15:22).
new: 2 Esdras 7:29 — *shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men that have life.* The library's universal death, then the raising; *as in Adam all die, even so in Messiah (Christ) shall all be made alive* (1 Corinthians 15:22).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God)... their hope is full of immortality* the seeming-death the sowing, immortality the raising; *sown in dishonour; raised in glory* (1 Corinthians 15:43).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* The seeming death is the sowing and the raising the harvest; *sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption* (1 Corinthians 15:42).

old: Sirach 23:9 — *accustom not thy mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One* the wisdom-library almost in James's words; not the oath abolished but the Name honored (James 5:12).
new: Ecclesiasticus 23:9 — *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* The wisdom library almost in James's words; not the oath abolished but the Name honored (James 5:12).

old: Sirach 38:9 — *in thy sickness... pray unto Yahuah (God), and he will make thee whole* the wisdom-library's medicine of the soul; *Is any sick among you? let him... pray* (James 5:14).
new: Ecclesiasticus 38:9 — *in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The wisdom library's medicine of the soul; *Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him* (James 5:14).

old: Tobit 12:9 — *alms doth deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin* righteous love that delivers from death; *shall save a soul from death* (James 5:20).
new: Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* Righteous love that delivers from death; *shall save a soul from death* (James 5:20).

old: ★ *delivered me... by the greatness of your name... out of the hands of such as sought after my life* (Sirach 51:3) — delivered by the Name (54:1) from those who *seek after my soul* (54:3).
