new: ★ *delivered me, according to the multitude of your mercies and greatness of your name* (Ecclesiasticus 51:3) — delivered by the Name (Psalm 54:1) from those who *seek after my soul* (Psalm 54:3).

old: ★ *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God)... in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (Wisdom 3:1,7) — the end seen in the sanctuary (73:17): the righteous held safe, only seeming to die.
new: ★ *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1) — the end seen in the sanctuary (Psalm 73:17): the righteous held safe, only seeming to die.

old: *A faithful friend is a strong defence... has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14) — the restored witness echoes 18:24; the true friend is a fortress and a treasure found.
new: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure* (Ecclesiasticus 6:14) — the restored witness echoes Proverbs 18:24; the true friend is a fortress and a treasure found.

old: ★ *thou feddest thy own people with angels' food... bread prepared without their labour* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20) — the restored wisdom sings the very phrase of 78:25.
new: ★ *you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20) — the restored wisdom sings the very phrase of Psalm 78:25.

old: ★ *they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob... and began to slay and destroy the people* (1 Maccabees 5:2) — the very plot of 83:4 to cut the people off from being a nation.
new: ★ *they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that was among them* (1 Maccabees 5:2) — the very plot of Psalm 83:4 to cut the people off from being a nation.

old: ★ *all nations shall praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people* (Tobit 14:7) — the nations come IN to His people (Zechariah 8:23); His people exalted, not replaced.
new: ★ *So shall all nations praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people* (Tobit 14:7) — the nations take hold of the skirt of a Yahudi (Jew) to go with him (Zechariah 8:23); his people exalted, not replaced.

old: ★ *entered into it... with branches of palm trees... and hymns, and songs* (1 Maccabees 13:51) — the palm-branch entry into Jerusalem; the rejoicing the daughter of Zion would pour on her true King (Zechariah 9:9).
new: ★ *with thanksgiving, and branches of palm trees, and with harps, and cymbals, and with viols, and hymns, and songs* (1 Maccabees 13:51) — the palm-branch entry into Jerusalem; the rejoicing the daughter of Zion would pour on her true King (Zechariah 9:9).

old: ★ *he will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5) — the regathering *from sea to sea* (Micah 7:12) is the two-house people brought home.
new: ★ *will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5) — the regathering *from sea to sea* (Micah 7:12) is the two-house people brought home.

old: ★ *Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea... and gave them a great overthrow* (1 Maccabees 5:3) — the recompense returns on the brother-line; the deed done to Jacob repaid (Obadiah 1:10).
new: ★ *Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea at Arabattine* (1 Maccabees 5:3) — he gave them a great overthrow; the recompense returns on the brother-line, the deed done to Jacob repaid (Obadiah 1:10).

old: *all nations shall praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people* (Tobit 14:7) — the ingathering of the stranger does not displace the people; both rejoice (1 Kings 8:43).
new: *So shall all nations praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people* (Tobit 14:7) — the stranger who prays toward the house is heard, and the people are exalted, not displaced (1 Kings 8:43).

old: *O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the throne of your glory... that she may labour with me* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:10) — wisdom descends from Yahuah's throne to enable the shepherd-king.
new: *send her out of your holy heavens, and from the throne of your glory* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:10) — wisdom comes down from the throne of Yahuah (God) to labour with the king who asked for it (2 Chronicles 1:10).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *thou feddest thy own people with angels' food... bread prepared without their labour*: the restored witness names the manna (Nehemiah 9:20).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour*: the restored witness names the manna (Nehemiah 9:20).

old: Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 18:11 — *Yahuah (God) is patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them*: the restored wisdom witnesses Nehemiah 9:17.
new: Ecclesiasticus 18:11 — *Therefore is Yahuah (God) patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.* The restored wisdom witnesses the Elohim (God) ready to pardon, slow to anger (Nehemiah 9:17).

old: Luke 6:44 -> Sirach 27:6 — *the fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* Luke 6:44's *every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs* names the fruit-test as the means of knowing; the Hebrew library named the fruit-declares-the-tree diagnostic.
new: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* The tree is known by what it brings forth and the heart by what its mouth speaks; *every tree is known by his own fruit* (Luke 6:44).

old: 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:40 — *those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive.* The wisdom-stream names the scattered by the precise history of the Assyrian captivity; Mark 13:27 gathers the same tribes home from the uttermost parts.
new: 2 Esdras 13:40 — *the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land.* The tribes named by the history of their scattering are the elect the angels gather *from the uttermost part of the earth* (Mark 13:27).

old: Baruch 4:36 — *O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* The face turned east to behold the gathering-joy; Luke 13:29's come-from-east-and-west walks the same prophetic-gathering register.
new: Baruch 4:36 — *look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* Jerusalem's face turned east toward the coming; the scattered children of Yashar'el (Israel) *shall come from the east, and from the west* to sit down in the kingdom (Luke 13:29).

old: Baruch 4:37 — *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One.* The sent-away sons regathered from the quarters; Luke 13:29's come-from-east-and-west names the same scattered children coming home — not strangers added.
new: Baruch 4:37 — *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west.* The sent-away sons coming home, not strangers added; *they shall come from the east, and from the west* (Luke 13:29).

old: Sirach 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Wisdom's come-and-be-filled call is the same invitation Yahusha (Jesus) extends at John 4:10 — *if thou knewest the gift of Elohim (God) ... he would have given thee living water.*
new: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Wisdom's call to come and be filled is the offer at the well, *he would have given thee living water* (John 4:10).

old: Tobit 11:11 — *he strake of the gall on his fathers' eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father.* The eyes-opened-by-the-appointed-means architecture; John 9:7's *go, wash in the pool of Siloam ... and came seeing* walks the same.
new: Tobit 11:11 — *he strake of the gall on his fathers’ eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father.* Sight restored by the means appointed; the man born blind *washed, and came seeing* (John 9:7).

old: Tobit 11:14 — *Blessed art you, O Yahuah (God), and blessed is your name for ever.* The blessing-of-the-name at the restored sight; John 9:38's *Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him* walks the same — worship of the Son of Elohim (God) who opened the eyes.
new: Tobit 11:14 — *Blessed art you, O Yahuah (God), and blessed is your name for ever.* The name blessed the moment sight returns; the man whose eyes were opened said *Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him* (John 9:38).

old: 1 Maccabees 9:30 — *Now therefore we have chosen you this day to be our prince and captain in his stead, that you may fight our battles.* The same acclamation once given to Jonathan now passes to Simon in 1-maccabees 13:8 — the remnant's leadership handed brother to brother, unbroken.
new: 1 Maccabees 9:30 — *we have chosen you this day to be our prince and captain in his stead.* The acclamation given to Jonathan passes to Simon, *You shall be our leader instead of Judas and Jonathan your brother* (1 Maccabees 13:8).

old: John 15:13 — *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* Simon's refusal to spare his own life for the nation in 1-maccabees 13:5 is the shape of the love the Messiah names and then perfects.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:5 — *be it far from me, that I should spare my own life in any time of trouble.* Simon's refusal to spare himself for the nation is the shape of the love the Messiah (Christ) names, *that a man lay down his life for his friends* (John 15:13).

old: Zechariah 9:13 — *When I have bent Yahudah (Judah) for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.* The people pledging Simon to fight their battles in 1-maccabees 13:9 is the prophet's bow of Judah bent against the sons of Greece.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:9 — *Fight you our battles, and whatsoever, you commandest us, that will we do.* The people pledging Simon to fight is the bow of Yahudah (Judah) bent against the sons of Greece (Zechariah 9:13).

old: 1 Maccabees 2:50 — *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* Simon's reckoning in 1-maccabees 13:3 of all the house has done for the laws and the sanctuary is the fulfilment of Mattathias' dying charge.
new: 1 Maccabees 2:50 — *be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* Mattathias' dying charge, which Simon reckons fulfilled in all his house has done *for the laws and the sanctuary* (1 Maccabees 13:3).

old: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* The brothers slain for Israel's sake in 1-maccabees 13:4 carry the priestly zeal of Phinehas, who stood for the covenant.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:4 — *all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake, and I am left alone.* The brothers who died for the covenant carry the zeal of Phinehas, who turned the wrath away (Numbers 25:11).

old: Hebrews 11:35 — *Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:* The brothers slain in 1-maccabees 13:4 are among those tortured who looked past deliverance to the better resurrection.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:4 — *all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake, and I am left alone.* The slain brothers are among those who were tortured, not accepting deliverance, *that they might obtain a better resurrection* (Hebrews 11:35).

old: 2 Maccabees 7:9 — *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* The hope behind the brothers' deaths in 1-maccabees 13:4 is voiced plainly by the martyr brother under the same persecution.
new: 2 Maccabees 7:9 — *the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* The hope behind the deaths of Simon's brothers, spoken plainly by the martyr under the same persecution (1 Maccabees 13:4).

old: Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Daniel had already sealed the everlasting life that crowns the brothers fallen for Israel in 1-maccabees 13:4.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:4 — *all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake, and I am left alone.* Daniel had already sealed the everlasting life that crowns them, *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake* (Daniel 12:2).

old: Leviticus 25:10 — *And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family.* Israel's new reckoning from the first year of Simon in 1-maccabees 13:42 is the jubilee proclamation of liberty written into their dating itself.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:42 — *In the first year of Simon the high priest, the governor and leader of the Yahudim (Jews).* Yashar'el (Israel) writing a new reckoning into its contracts is liberty proclaimed in the land, the pattern of the jubile (Leviticus 25:10).

old: Isaiah 9:4 — *For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.* The heathen yoke taken away in 1-maccabees 13:41 is the broken yoke Isaiah sang of in the day of the Child to be born.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:41 — *the yoke of the heathen was taken away from Yashar'el (Israel) in the hundred and seventieth year.* The yoke lifted is the one Isaiah sang broken, *the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder* (Isaiah 9:4).

old: Isaiah 10:27 — *And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing.* The yoke destroyed because of the anointing answers the heathen yoke lifted from Israel in 1-maccabees 13:41.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:41 — *the yoke of the heathen was taken away from Yashar'el (Israel).* The yoke lifted answers *the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing* (Isaiah 10:27).

old: Isaiah 14:25 — *That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.* Yahuah's pledge to break the oppressor and lift the burden from the shoulder is realized when the yoke departs from Israel in 1-maccabees 13:41.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:41 — *Thus the yoke of the heathen was taken away from Yashar'el (Israel).* The pledge to break the oppressor so that *his yoke depart from off them* is seen kept (Isaiah 14:25).

old: John 10:22 — *And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.* Simon's ordaining the day of the cleansed citadel to be kept every year in 1-maccabees 13:52 belongs to the same feast of dedication the Messiah Himself kept in Jerusalem.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:52 — *He ordained also that that day should be kept every year with gladness.* The cleansed citadel's yearly day belongs with *the feast of the dedication* the Messiah (Christ) kept in Jerusalem (John 10:22).

old: Ezekiel 36:25 — *Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.* Simon cleansing the houses of the idols in 1-maccabees 13:47 enacts the promised cleansing of the covenant people from their idols.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:47 — *cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and so entered into it with songs and thanksgiving.* Simon's cleansing enacts the promise, *from all your idols, will I cleanse you* (Ezekiel 36:25).

old: Isaiah 52:1 — *Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean.* Simon putting all uncleanness out and setting law-keepers there in 1-maccabees 13:48 is the holy city into which the unclean shall come no more.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:48 — *he put all uncleanness out of it, and placed such men there as would keep the law.* The purged stronghold of law-keepers is the holy city into which *there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean* (Isaiah 52:1).

old: Zechariah 14:21 — *Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Yahudah (Judah) shall be holiness unto Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* Simon's purged stronghold of law-keepers in 1-maccabees 13:48 foreshadows the day when all Jerusalem is holiness and no defiled thing remains.
new: 1 Maccabees 13:48 — *he put all uncleanness out of it, and placed such men there as would keep the law.* A foreshadow of the day when *every pot in Jerusalem and in Yahudah (Judah) shall be holiness unto Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Zechariah 14:21).

old: Deuteronomy 10:18 — *He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.* Yahuah Himself defends the cause whose relief was laid up in the house at 2-maccabees 3:10.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:10 — *there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.* The cause whose relief lay in the house is the cause Yahuah (God) himself takes up, *the judgment of the fatherless and widow* (Deuteronomy 10:18).

old: Joel 2:17 — *Let the priests, the ministers of Yahuah (LORD), weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Yahuah (LORD), and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their Elohim (God)?* The very prophetic liturgy the priests enact prostrate before the altar in 2-maccabees 3:15.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:15 — *the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven.* The very liturgy the prophet gave, *weep between the porch and the altar* (Joel 2:17).

old: Numbers 16:48 — *And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.* As Aaron's priestly standing turned back wrath, so the priests' supplication stands between the temple and the spoiler at 2-maccabees 3:15.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:15 — *the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven.* As Aaron *stood between the dead and the living* (Numbers 16:48), the priests' supplication stands between the house and the spoiler.

old: Psalm 127:1 — *Except Yahuah (LORD) build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.* The people commit the keeping to the Almighty in 2-maccabees 3:22 because no human watch can guard the house.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:22 — *called upon the Almighty Yahuah (God) to keep the things committed of trust safe and sure.* No human watch can guard the house; *except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain* (Psalm 127:1).

old: Joshua 5:14 — *And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of Yahuah (LORD) am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?* The Prince of all power who causes the apparition in 2-maccabees 3:24 is the captain of Yahuah's host come to defend His own.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:24 — *the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition.* All who presumed to come in with Heliodorus were astonished; the Prince of all power is the *captain of the host of Yahuah (LORD)* who met Joshua (Joshua 5:14).

old: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* The same heaven that smote Assyria for besieging Jerusalem strikes Heliodorus' host in 2-maccabees 3:24.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:24 — *astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.* The same heaven that smote the Assyrian camp before Jerusalem strikes Heliodorus' guard (2 Kings 19:35).

old: 2 Chronicles 32:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) sent an angel, which cut off all the mighty men of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land...* As one angel cut off Sennacherib's captains, so the apparition routs the king's treasurer in 2-maccabees 3:24.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:24 — *astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.* As one angel cut off Sennacherib's captains, the apparition routs the king's treasurer (2 Chronicles 32:21).

old: Psalm 35:5 — *Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of Yahuah (LORD) chase them.* The fiercely running rider of 2-maccabees 3:25 is the chasing angel the psalmist summoned against the oppressors of the righteous.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:25 — *he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet.* The fiercely running rider is the chasing angel the psalmist summoned, *let the angel of Yahuah (LORD) chase them* (Psalm 35:5).

old: Acts 9:3 — *And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:* As light from heaven felled the persecutor Saul, the dread apparition compasses Heliodorus with great darkness and casts him down in 2-maccabees 3:27.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:27 — *Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness.* As light from heaven felled Saul on the Damascus road, darkness fells the spoiler of the house (Acts 9:3).

old: Acts 9:4 — *And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?* Like Saul thrown to the earth and then made a herald, Heliodorus falls suddenly and is sent to declare the power he fought, in 2-maccabees 3:27,34.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:27 — *Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness.* Like Saul thrown to the earth and then made a herald, Heliodorus falls and is sent to declare the power he fought (Acts 9:4).

old: Psalm 76:7 — *Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?* Heliodorus lies cast down and speechless in 2-maccabees 3:29 because no man may stand before the wrath of Yahuah.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:29 — *he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.* No man may stand before his anger; *who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?* (Psalm 76:7).

old: 2 Maccabees 9:5 — *But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;* The treasurer Heliodorus is felled and spared at a priest's prayer in 2-maccabees 3:27, but the unrepentant Antiochus who likewise raged against the sanctuary is struck without remedy.
new: 2 Maccabees 9:5 — *struck him with an incurable and invisible plague.* Heliodorus was felled and spared at a priest's prayer (2 Maccabees 3:27); the unrepentant Antiochus who raged against the sanctuary is struck without remedy.

old: Psalm 127:1 — *Except Yahuah (LORD) build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.* Heliodorus confesses in 2-maccabees 3:39 that He who dwells in heaven keeps the place no man's labour could defend.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:39 — *he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it.* Heliodorus confesses what the psalm sings, *except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain* (Psalm 127:1).

old: Zechariah 2:5 — *For I, saith Yahuah (LORD), will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her.* The God who keeps His eye on the place and beats off its enemies in 2-maccabees 3:39 is the wall of fire round His city.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:39 — *he beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it.* The one who keeps his eye on the place is *a wall of fire round about* his city (Zechariah 2:5).

old: Isaiah 31:5 — *As birds flying, so will Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.* The LORD who defends and preserves Jerusalem is the same that defendeth His place against all who would hurt it in 2-maccabees 3:39.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:39 — *he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it.* The same Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) who will *defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it* (Isaiah 31:5).

old: 2 Thessalonians 1:6 — *Seeing it is a righteous thing with Elohim (God) to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you;* The well-scourged spoiler of 2-maccabees 3:38 shows the righteous recompense the apostle promises to all who trouble the covenant people — it ain't new.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:38 — *send him thither, and you shall receive him well scourged, if he escape with his life.* The well-scourged spoiler shows the recompense the apostle promises, *a righteous thing with Elohim (God) to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you* (2 Thessalonians 1:6).

old: Leviticus 23:40 — *And ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and ye shall rejoice before Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) seven days.* The branches, boughs, and palms the Maccabees bore in 2-maccabees 10:7 are the prescribed Sukkot rite of Torah, kept out of season because they had been hunted in the mountains.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:7 — *they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms.* The tabernacles rite of Torah, *branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees* (Leviticus 23:40), kept out of season because they had been hunted in the mountains.

old: Nehemiah 8:15 — *And that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, Go forth unto the mount, and fetch olive branches, and pine branches, and myrtle branches, and palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make booths, as it is written.* As the returned remnant under Ezra rediscovered the booths-feast and proclaimed it, so the Maccabees in 2-maccabees 10:6 keep tabernacles as a people lately delivered out of the wilderness of dens and beasts.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:6 — *they kept the eight days with gladness, as in the feast of the tabernacles.* As the returned remnant under Ezra proclaimed the booths again (Nehemiah 8:15), the Maccabees keep tabernacles as a people lately out of the dens.

old: John 10:22 — *And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.* The yearly winter feast the whole nation ordained in 2-maccabees 10:8 is the very Feast of Dedication the Messiah kept in the temple — He honoured the Maccabean rededication.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:8 — *every year those days should be kept of the whole nation of the Yahudim (Jews).* The yearly winter feast the nation ordained is *the feast of the dedication* the Messiah (Christ) kept at Jerusalem (John 10:22).

old: 1 Maccabees 4:59 — *Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.* The brother book records the same eight-day statute on the twenty-fifth of Casleu that 2-maccabees 10:8 decrees for the whole nation.
new: 1 Maccabees 4:59 — *the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year.* The brother book records the same eight-day statute from the twenty-fifth of Casleu (2 Maccabees 10:8).

old: Zechariah 14:16 — *And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and to keep the feast of tabernacles.* The tabernacles-keeping with palms and psalms in 2-maccabees 10:7 prefigures the day all nations go up yearly to keep that same feast before the King.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:7 — *they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms.* Tabernacles kept with palms and psalms, before the day all that are left of the nations go up yearly *to keep the feast of tabernacles* (Zechariah 14:16).

old: Daniel 11:31 — *And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.* The heathen altars and chapels the Maccabees pull down in 2-maccabees 10:2 are exactly the abomination Daniel foresaw Antiochus placing in the polluted sanctuary.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:2 — *the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down.* The heathen altars pulled down are *the abomination that maketh desolate* Daniel saw placed in the polluted sanctuary (Daniel 11:31).

old: Daniel 8:13 — *Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot?* The cleansing on the very day of the profanation in 2-maccabees 10:5 answers the angel's 'how long' over the trodden sanctuary.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:5 — *upon the same day that the strangers profaned the temple, on the very same day it was cleansed again.* The cleansing on the day of the profaning answers the saint's question, *How long shall be the vision* (Daniel 8:13).

old: Matthew 24:15 — *When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:)* The recovery of the defiled temple in 2-maccabees 10:1 is the historical first fulfillment of the abomination the Messiah warns will yet stand in the holy place.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:1 — *Maccabeus and his company, Yahuah (God) guiding them, recovered the temple and the city.* The temple Maccabeus recovers is the one Antiochus had defiled — the first standing of *the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet*, which the Messiah (Christ) warns will yet stand again in the holy place (Matthew 24:15).

old: 2 Samuel 24:14 — *And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of Yahuah (the LORD); for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.* David's choice to fall into Yahuah's merciful hand rather than man's is precisely the prayer of 2-maccabees 10:4 — chasten us, but spare us the blasphemous nations.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:4 — *if they sinned any more against him, that he himself would chasten them with mercy.* David chose the hand of Yahuah (LORD) over the hand of man, *let us fall now into the hand of Yahuah (LORD); for his mercies are great* (2 Samuel 24:14), and the Maccabees pray the same.

old: Tobit 13:5 — *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* Tobit voices the same covenant confidence the Maccabees pray in 2-maccabees 10:4 — the chastening of the scattered people ends in mercy and regathering, not abandonment.
new: Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations.* The same covenant confidence the Maccabees pray, that chastening ends in mercy and not in abandonment (2 Maccabees 10:4).

old: Hebrews 8:12 — *For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.* The very mercy the Maccabees ask to be chastened with in 2-maccabees 10:4 is the covenant promise — corrected in mercy, their sins not held against them.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:4 — *if they sinned any more against him, that he himself would chasten them with mercy.* The mercy they ask to be chastened with is the covenant promise, *I will be merciful to their unrighteousness* (Hebrews 8:12).

old: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The everlasting covenant given for Phinehas' zeal is the inheritance the zealous Maccabean house claims as it burns out the blasphemers in 2-maccabees 10:36.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:36 — *burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive.* The zeal that burns out the blasphemers claims the covenant given for Phinehas' zeal, *the covenant of an everlasting priesthood* (Numbers 25:13).

old: 2 Kings 6:17 — *And Elisha prayed, and said, Yahuah (LORD), I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And Yahuah (LORD) opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.* The five comely horsemen from heaven who shield Maccabeus in 2-maccabees 10:29 are the same heavenly cavalry Elisha's servant was given eyes to see.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:29 — *there appeared to the enemies from heaven five comely men upon horses, with bridles of gold.* The heavenly cavalry that shields Maccabeus is the host Elisha's servant was given eyes to see, *horses and chariots of fire* (2 Kings 6:17).

old: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* The psalms and thanksgiving with which the people praise Yahuah for the victory in 2-maccabees 10:38 reprise the song Moses sang when the LORD overthrew horse and rider.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:38 — *they praised Yahuah (God) with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Yashar'el (Israel).* The victory song reprises the song at the sea, *the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea* (Exodus 15:1).

old: Exodus 15:3 — *Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war: Yahuah (LORD) is his name.* The heavenly riders who shoot arrows and lightnings to deliver Maccabeus in 2-maccabees 10:30 make plain that the battle belongs to Yahuah the man of war.
new: 2 Maccabees 10:30 — *shot arrows and lightnings against the enemies: so that being confounded with blindness, and full of trouble, they were killed.* The riders who deliver Maccabeus make plain whose battle it is, *Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war* (Exodus 15:3).

old: Exodus 23:20 — *Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.* The good angel the Maccabees beg for in 2-maccabees 11:6 is the very Angel Yahuah pledged to send before His covenant people.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:6 — *besought Yahuah (God) that he would send a good angel to deliver Yashar'el (Israel).* The good angel they beg for is the Angel pledged to go before the people, *Behold, I send an Angel before thee* (Exodus 23:20).

old: Exodus 23:22 — *But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.* The condition of that heavenly help is covenant obedience — the very Torah-faithfulness for which the men of 2-maccabees 11:6 are fighting.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:6 — *with lamentation and tears besought Yahuah (God) that he would send a good angel.* The help is promised to obedience, *if thou shalt indeed obey his voice* (Exodus 23:22), the Torah faithfulness these men are fighting for.

old: Joshua 5:13 — *And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?* The same drawn-armed Figure that met Joshua at Jericho rides before the Maccabees at Jerusalem in 2-maccabees 11:8.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:8 — *there appeared before them on horseback one in white clothing, shaking his armour of gold.* The same armed figure who met Joshua at Jericho *with his sword drawn in his hand* (Joshua 5:13) rides before the Maccabees.

old: Joshua 5:14 — *And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of Yahuah (LORD) am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?* The white-clad horseman of 2-maccabees 11:8 is that Captain of the host of Yahuah, come to lead Israel's battle.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:8 — *there appeared before them on horseback one in white clothing, shaking his armour of gold.* The white-clad horseman is the *captain of the host of Yahuah (LORD)* come to lead the battle (Joshua 5:14).

old: 2 Maccabees 3:25 — *For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.* The golden-harnessed rider who smote Heliodorus at the temple is the same heavenly horseman who now leads Israel in 2-maccabees 11:8.
new: 2 Maccabees 3:25 — *it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.* The golden-harnessed rider who smote Heliodorus at the temple is the horseman who now leads Yashar'el (Israel) (2 Maccabees 11:8).

old: Revelation 19:11 — *And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.* The white horseman shaking his golden armour in 2-maccabees 11:8 foreshadows the Rider Faithful and True who leads the armies of heaven.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:8 — *one in white clothing, shaking his armour of gold.* The white horseman foreshadows the Rider *called Faithful and True* who judges and makes war (Revelation 19:11).

old: 2 Kings 6:17 — *And Elisha prayed, and said, Yahuah (LORD), I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And Yahuah (LORD) opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.* The helper from heaven seen marching with Israel in 2-maccabees 11:10 is that same unseen host of fiery horses and chariots.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:10 — *they marched forward in their armour, having an helper from heaven.* The helper from heaven is the unseen host, *horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha* (2 Kings 6:17).

old: 2 Kings 6:16 — *And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.* Lysias' own conclusion in 2-maccabees 11:13 that the Hebrews could not be overcome is the enemy's-eye proof of Elisha's word — heaven's host outnumbers every army of men.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:13 — *the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty Yahuah (God) helped them.* The enemy's own conclusion proves Elisha's word, *they that be with us are more than they that be with them* (2 Kings 6:16).

old: Revelation 19:14 — *And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.* The Almighty who could not be resisted in 2-maccabees 11:13 is He whose heavenly armies ride behind Him in white at the last.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:13 — *the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty Yahuah (God) helped them.* The Almighty who cannot be resisted is the one *the armies which were in heaven followed* at the last (Revelation 19:14).

old: Psalm 119:44 — *So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever.* The manner of living the Jews would not surrender in 2-maccabees 11:24 is exactly this enduring delight to keep Yahuah's law for ever.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:24 — *had rather keep their own manner of living.* The manner of living the Yahudim (Jews) would not surrender is the delight of the psalm, *So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever* (Psalm 119:44).

old: 2 Maccabees 7:9 — *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* The laws Antiochus is forced to restore in 2-maccabees 11:24 are the very laws the seven brothers died for, in the hope of resurrection.
new: 2 Maccabees 7:9 — *the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* The laws the king is forced to let them keep (2 Maccabees 11:24) are the laws the seven brothers died for, in hope of the resurrection.

old: Hebrews 11:35 — *Women received their dead raised to life again: and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection.* The Maccabean refusal to abandon their own meats and laws in 2-maccabees 11:31 is the very faith Hebrews crowns with the better resurrection.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:31 — *the Yahudim (Jews) shall use their own kind of meats and laws, as before.* The refusal to abandon their meats and laws is the faith Hebrews crowns, *that they might obtain a better resurrection* (Hebrews 11:35).

old: Ezra 7:25 — *And thou, Ezra, after the wisdom of thy Elohim (God), that is in thine hand, set magistrates and judges, which may judge all the people that are beyond the river, all such as know the laws of thy Elohim (God); and teach ye them that know them not.* As Persia once decreed the restoration of Yahuah's law over His people, so the king's letter in 2-maccabees 11:25 is forced to restore the temple and the customs of the forefathers.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:25 — *restore them their temple, that they may live according to the customs of their forefathers.* As Persia once decreed the law of Elohim (God) set over his people (Ezra 7:25), the king's letter is forced to restore the temple and the fathers' customs.

old: John 10:22 — *And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.* The temple restored to the Jews in 2-maccabees 11:25 is the house whose rededication became the very feast the Messiah Himself kept at Jerusalem.
new: 2 Maccabees 11:25 — *we have determined to restore them their temple.* The restored house is the one whose rededication became *the feast of the dedication* the Messiah (Christ) kept (John 10:22).

old: Wisdom of Solomon 5:18 — *He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet* the wisdom-tradition's armour-of-the-righteous; the same breastplate and helmet the children of the day put on (1 Thessalonians 5:8).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 5:18 — *He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet.* The armour the righteous Deliverer wears is what the children of the day put on, *the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation* (1 Thessalonians 5:8).

old: ★ *he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again* (Tobit 13:2) — the library's own thanksgiving prayer prays the exact brought-up-from-Sheol motion of 30:3.
new: Tobit 13:2 — *he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand.* The library's thanksgiving prays the same motion as David, *thou hast brought up my soul from the grave* (Psalm 30:3).

old: ★ *who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1) — the second-Temple prayer confesses the psalm's own creation-by-the-Word (33:6).
new: Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word.* Solomon's prayer confesses the psalm's own creation by the Word, *By the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made* (Psalm 33:6).

old: the-rest-of-esther 13:4 — *Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.* The Greek decree of Artaxerxes frames the same accusation as 3 Macc 3:7 — a people whose laws set them apart is named an enemy of the realm.
new: The Rest of Esther 13:4 — *there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations.* Artaxerxes' decree frames the same accusation as 3 Maccabees 3:7, a people set apart by their laws named an enemy of the realm.

old: the-rest-of-esther 13:6 — *Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:* The Greek text of Artaxerxes' decree matches 3 Macc 3:25 phrase for phrase — total destruction of the people *with wives and children*.
new: The Rest of Esther 13:6 — *with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity.* The decree matches 3 Maccabees 3:25 phrase for phrase, total destruction *with wives and children*.

old: Sirach 48:1 — *Elias the prophet as fire... he shut up the heaven* (48:1,3) the Hebrew library's memory of Elias; the prophet whose earnest prayer governed the rain (James 5:17).
new: Sirach 48:1–3 — *Elias the prophet as fire... he shut up the heaven* the Hebrew library's memory of Elias; the prophet whose earnest prayer governed the rain (James 5:17).
